By employing the tools we developed, we demonstrate the potential for significant privacy risks during social studies, even when researchers' actions are well-intentioned. Our research highlights the importance of considering privacy implications in academic studies.

We are examining a scenario where a system of independent branching particles is influenced by random fluctuations in death rates, originating from an initial population of $n$ identical particles within a shared branching space. Our focus lies on the timing of the event when two or more particles merge, which is of particular interest. Under the assumption that each particle's reproductive and death rates are independent and follow identical normal distributions, our research reveals that as the initial population size $n$ approaches infinity, the time until the first particle death-synchronization is accurately approximated by a non-stationary gamma distribution. Furthermore, we derive the moment sequence of this distribution, which is defined by a specific type of equation that describes the evolution of the mean time until the first particle death-synchronization. This equation is also seen to describe the evolution of the mean time until synchronized death-synchronization in a system of interacting branching particles with a death rate that fluctuates randomly.

In a two-dimensional lattice model, we investigate a spin model with a non-finite number of spin values, which is not enumerable. This model is connected to a HC (homogeneous tree) model and retains its periodic translation symmetry. Our study indicates the existence of an unlimited number of distinct Gibbs measures that differ in their free energy values based on the spin value $s$. We also discover that the Gibbs measures with higher free energy values correspond to stronger mixing within the set of spin values. Furthermore, we find that the Gibbs measures with lower free energy values exclusively focus on the spin value $1$. This model is constructed using a method that combines a HC model approach with a model-based approach, originating from Federico Matuso's work.

We introduce a new catalog of 66,379 galaxies from LAMOST-DR7 with reliable velocity dispersion data. The galaxies were selected based on four distinct criteria: having at least 20 pixels in their velocity distribution, a velocity dispersion of at least 15 km s$^{-1}$, a signal-to-noise ratio of five or higher, and four or more pixels in their dispersion distribution. By applying these strict criteria, we achieved a high level of accuracy in our results, with a median error in our mock samples of 2.2 km s$^{-1}$. The catalog of galaxies with velocity dispersion data has a high success rate, with 85% of the galaxies falling within 1$\sigma$ of their true velocity dispersion. The galaxies in our catalog fall within a specific mass range of $10^{7.3}$ to $10^{11.3}$ M$_{\odot}$, and their velocity dispersions do not show a strong correlation with the signal-to-noise ratio. The catalog of galaxies with velocity dispersion data is also free from contamination by binary stars and active galactic nuclei, with only 0.5% of the galaxies potentially hosting active galactic nuclei. The galaxies in our catalog have a high level of accuracy in their morphological classifications, with a high level of agreement between their visual and automated classifications.

In a research paper, novel variations in indium isotopes were studied using a highly advanced, multireference many-body approach. By employing the Reaction Relativistic Coupled-Cluster Method with full configuration interaction, in its full and no-pair forms, in conjunction with the Separable Pair Transformation, theoretical predictions of ground state energies, low-lying excitation energies, and various reaction properties for 4 distinct isotopes were generated. Notably, the present findings indicate that the ground state energies and low-lying excitation energies are accurately described by the no-pair RRCCM, and that the inclusion of pair correlations through the SRPT significantly enhances the predicted energy differences between the ground states of isotopes with mass variations of approximately $\pm 40$. Moreover, the study revealed that the SRPT can effectively predict the trend of quadrupole moment in isotopes with varying masses, and that the RRCCM can accurately predict the potential energy barriers for $\alpha$-decay and $\beta$-delayed neutron release in isotopes with mass variations of up to $\pm 40$.

In quantum mechanics, graph states are significant because they are stable under specific types of quantum measurements and serve as a foundation for quantum networks. A graph state can be identified by the signs of the principal minors of its associated connection matrix, which determines its stability. This research expands on existing knowledge by establishing relationships among families of graph states studied in the past, through patterns in the signs of the principal minors of their associated connection matrices. This connection allows us to recognize which states are stable and which require more complex quantum measurements. Furthermore, we explore a novel family of graph states with unique properties and show they cannot be created using a simpler quantum process.

A configuration in a n-element set, denoted as (N, L), consists of two distinct subsets N and L, both containing the same number of elements (where n is at least 2). A line is considered present in this configuration if a single-element subset of N satisfies the condition that its intersection with L has exactly one element. A configuration is classified as having transversals if any two distinct lines can be found that intersect at exactly one element. This study presents a condition for the presence of transversals in these configurations: if a particular subset of N, containing the minimum of n/2 or k (where k is the number of lines in N), can be divided into groups such that each group's intersection with L has no more than one element, then any two lines in N have a point in common. Furthermore, this result resolves a long-standing conjecture by Chv\'atal and Erd\H{o}s and leads to the conclusion that any such configuration with the minimum number of lines (n/2) contains a transversal.

Video transcoding is an essential process for creating versatile video content and offers various applications in multiple domains. However, its high complexity complicates the task of optimizing performance. To achieve optimal results, this research investigates the most effective approach for video transcoding on cloud-based systems. By leveraging cloud computing's resource flexibility, video transcoding can significantly accelerate processing times, making it more practical for large-scale projects. In this study, a novel video transcoding framework was developed to maximize performance gains. To further reduce wait times, resource scheduling algorithms were also designed to efficiently allocate cloud resources. Through simulations and real-world testing, server configuration optimization was demonstrated to yield superior performance. Moreover, a new resource scheduling algorithm was proposed to efficiently allocate cloud resources. The results of this work will contribute to advancing resource scheduling techniques for video-based applications in cloud computing.

In studying cycle spaces of graphs, our attention is focused on variations that fall within a moderate range, with a mid-point value of 1. We demonstrate that a moderate alteration to a cycle space will always result in a subspace. Moreover, for connected graphs, the subspace resulting from such a moderate alteration is necessarily distinct unless the original graph possesses only two cycles in its cycle space.

We investigate the basic state solutions of the energy-superior Gross--Pitaevskii equation, denoted as $P$. This equation is given by $i\partial_t u=-|u|^2u -|u|^{p}$, where the nonlinearity term $-|u|^{p}$ with $p>4$ in three or more dimensions causes the basic state solutions to exhibit blow-up. We examine the Morse index of the basic state solutions $u_0(x,t)=\sqrt{\frac{1}{\lambda}\rho_0(x)}e^{-i|Alexandru's Conjecture|}$, where the basic state solutions are given by $u_0(x)=\sqrt{\frac{1}{\lambda}\rho_0(x)}e^{-i\lambda t}$. The existence of a non-zero Morse index for the basic state solutions $u_0$ indicates that the limit solution contains singular points. We find that the Morse index of the basic state solutions $u_0$ is at least one, and in certain cases, we can calculate the exact Morse index for the basic state solutions $u_0$.

This paper proposes a comprehensive method to develop a rigorous structure for automated evaluation of design quality in educational settings, specifically for survey designs. We aim to minimize the risk of Type I errors, which occur when a design fails to differentiate between intended groups in the survey questions. Our approach is divided into two stages. In the first stage, we employ a systematic process to identify all possible design configurations, eliminating those that do not meet the Type I error criteria. In the second stage, we analyze these remaining designs to minimize the likelihood of statistical error, defined as the probability of incorrectly assuming the presence of group differences when it actually exists. We also explore the use of machine learning and efficient set algorithms to streamline this process. Our method is applied to a case study involving survey questions about extracurricular activities.

We introduce DHR, a distributed system for collective real-time rendering that enables large-scale metaverse experiences through efficient rendering and user interaction. Building on virtual reality technology, DHR provides numerous benefits including more realistic interactions, customizable settings, and expanded access to the metaverse through various devices. Our system harnesses the collective computing power and rendering abilities of multiple devices, showcasing the potential of metaverse technology through real-time 3D renderings and a metaverse prototype.

This research paper presents novel methods to enhance the accuracy of music annotation and audio alignment, specifically tailored for complex orchestral music tracks. To optimize music annotation, we have developed an automated approach that leverages a neural network trained on partial human annotations to estimate the remaining musical notes. Moreover, our proposed method for audio alignment technique utilizes a neural network to predict the synchronization interval between two music tracks, thus facilitating the alignment process. Through a series of experiments, we have demonstrated the effectiveness of our proposed methods in both music annotation and audio alignment scenarios.

In recent years, in-band full-duplex radios have garnered significant attention for their potential to significantly boost energy efficiency and enable new applications. However, self-interference remains a major challenge in implementing these systems. Existing research has primarily focused on mitigating this interference and has proposed various solutions, such as joint precoding and equalization techniques and multi-antenna architectures. This work presents an innovative framework that integrates sophisticated self-interference mitigation and multi-antenna techniques. Specifically, we develop a family of advanced filter designs that combine transceiver filtering with multi-antenna architectures and compare their performance to conventional methods. Our numerical results indicate that this integrated approach surpasses existing techniques in terms of performance and power consumption efficiency.

During the cooling and solidification of a colloidal droplet, a complex sequence of events unfolds.  The top layer of the droplet solidifies, causing the colloidal particles inside the liquid-rich region to experience capillary stress, leading to further particle settling and liquid draw-down.  As the solidification front progresses, a combination of capillary forces and strong inter-particle interactions triggers the bending and invagination of the liquid-rich colloidal suspension.  The resulting self-assembly structures exhibit a range of morphologies, from smooth and irregular to complex.  The underlying dynamics of this solidification process are not yet fully understood, although they are crucial in forming these distinct structures.  In this study, a combination of high-resolution imaging techniques, including optical microscopy and quantitative phase microscopy, is used to capture the complete solidification process.  The resulting images are then analyzed to provide a range of quantitative metrics, shedding light on the formation of these intriguing structures.  The experimental findings are also supported by numerical simulations, providing valuable insights into the physical mechanisms driving this self-assembly process.

A crucial factor in the formation of the first stars and quasars is the UV radiation produced by the young stars. However, the link between these stars and the UV emission in their surrounding disk environments remains unclear. This study examines the UV emission in the z=4.2 disk surrounding a galaxy core, known as SMACS J221737.3+013442. By analyzing images from the Hubble Space Telescope, researchers found that the UV emission in the disk is closely tied to the presence of gas and young stars. They found that the UV emission in the disk is significantly higher than in the core, with a ratio of approximately 10:1. This suggests that the young stars in the disk are producing more UV emission per unit mass of gas than the central galaxy core. Furthermore, the team found that the UV emission in the disk is strongly correlated with the density of young stars, with a direct proportionality relationship. This study provides a crucial link between UV emission and the physical properties of the disk environments, with implications for understanding the formation of stars and quasars.

In this research, we explore the potential of adaptive intelligent surfaces (IS) to enhance the performance of fingerprint-based location systems operating at millimeter wave frequencies. To leverage the unique propagation characteristics of multipath signals, we propose an efficient approach for constructing location fingerprints, which eliminates the need for extensive training processes. An IS is then employed to optimize the signal-to-noise ratio of received signals at a fixed reference point by adjusting the reflective surfaces of the IS. Experimental results, including simulations and outdoor measurements, are used to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method and demonstrate the advantages of adaptive IS over static surfaces in terms of location accuracy and IS complexity.

We suggest a new method of producing a twisted condensate through the application of a magnetic field on a mixture of cold magnetically responsive atoms, such as the $^{166}E$-$^{87}R$ system. This process creates a spinor condensate with equal particle density and spin components. By adjusting the magnetic field strength, we can control the level of spin-orbit coupling and topological features in the system. Our research demonstrates that this method produces a stable, twisted condensate with a twisted angle that can be manipulated by the magnetic field strength, encompassing a full range of twisted configurations. Furthermore, our findings indicate that an increase in the magnetic field results in a significant enhancement in the system's twisted phase stiffness.

The US electric vehicle market is poised to significantly grow due to the anticipated 2025 ban on gas-powered vehicles, leading to increased competition and higher adoption rates. To stay competitive, companies may install electric vehicle charging stations at their own facilities or with suppliers to offer customers a more convenient charging experience. However, implementing this infrastructure comes at a significant cost, estimated to be around $500,000 per station with ongoing maintenance expenses of around $40,000 per year. The cost of these charging stations is a major concern for both private and public companies, leading to a potential issue of market concentration. To address this concern, the Federal Trade Commission is tasked with enforcing antitrust laws, but certain policies, such as the Electric Vehicle Charging Station Resilience and Fairness Act, aim to promote fair market competition. In this paper, we present a location selection model to help companies determine the most optimal charging station site locations, taking into account the cost savings associated with reduced travel distances between vehicle owners and these stations. Utilizing a case study in the city of New York, we demonstrate that this model can identify the most suitable locations for charging stations, allowing companies to save up to 20% on costs. Furthermore, we analyze the implications of the 2025 ban on gas-powered vehicles on the market structure, highlighting the potential for increased competition. To address the associated market concentration concerns, we propose a market structure model that incorporates the existing and anticipated EV charging station market structure, highlighting the need for ant

In a multi-stage lottery with decreasing prize values, strategies to maximize the likelihood of achieving the highest possible payout are often compared under two distinct models: the fair-elimination tie-breaker and the optimal tie-breaker. The current study offers a detailed analysis of the ideal tie-breaker model by creating a structured hierarchy of tie-breaker designs, identifying both the minimum and maximum participation requirements for each tie-breaker, as well as the conditions necessary to achieve both the maximum and minimum levels of participation. Furthermore, the design hierarchy is utilized to investigate the impact of tie-breaker modifications on the overall expected outcome, examining both the loss in scenarios where the fair-elimination tie-breaker would result in a failure and the gain relative to the worst-case scenario of the worst-placing finisher.

In the context of the ${\mathcal N}=1$ superconformal theory framework, we examine three-point correlations of higher-spin spinor multiplets involving three supersymmetric partial derivatives of a complex field $Q_i$, denoted as ${\cal O}_{Q}^{{\cal F}_{-1}}$. This multiplet has a conformal dimension of $\frac{3l+2}{4}$ and is part of a superconformal multiplet of order $l+2$, where $l$ is a half-integer. Our results show that the three-point correlations are completely determined by the superconformal properties of the theory and are independent of the interactions, similar to those involving three-point correlations of scalar or conserved currents in ${\mathcal N}=4$ superconformal supermultiplets. This is because the three-point correlations are determined by the structure constants of superconformal supermultiplets, which are fully defined by the superconformal group's Casimir operators. We also found that the three-point correlations are completely determined by the superconformal properties of the theory and are independent of the interactions, similar to those involving three-point correlations of scalar or conserved currents in ${\mathcal N}=1$ superconformal framework.

Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have led to the development of 
machine instructions, which enable users to provide feedback on both content and 
its processing. Research on machine instructions has primarily been conducted by or 
in collaboration with adults, resulting in limited exploration of machine instructions 
among children. This is particularly concerning given that children are natural 
language learners and can benefit significantly from interactive technology. 
Therefore, this study aimed to investigate children's perceptions of machine 
instructions, including their characteristics, features, and potential applications, 
as well as their willingness to use them in schools. A survey was designed and 
interviews were conducted with 60 children aged 8-12 to gather more detailed insights 
and opinions. The results showed that children were generally enthusiastic about 
machine instructions, enjoyed interacting with them, and preferred their interactive 
nature over reading. They appreciated the ability to engage with complex topics, 
receive instant feedback, and ask questions. The findings also suggested that 
children were motivated by a desire to learn, enjoy interactive experiences, and 
improve their knowledge and problem-solving skills. The results of this study have 
implications for future research, including examining children's learning outcomes 
and identifying the most effective deployment of machine instructions in schools to 
maximize their benefits.

A fundamental assumption in traditional reinforcement learning is that an agent learns to maximize the cumulative expected reward over time, yet recent studies have introduced various agents using alternative reward optimization methods with different objective functions. Traditional agents like value-based and policy-based methods worked within the original framework of maximizing expected reward. However, agents utilizing deep learning and employing different optimization approaches at their core defy traditional categorization while achieving comparable results, often through non-monotonic training processes. This paper will explore the distinct optimization methods used by these agents and examine how they converge or diverge from traditional approaches.

We have developed a versatile method for on-chip waveguide conversion of photonic quantum signals between various dimensions of freedom, including different waveforms, polarization states, and spectral frequencies. This technique enables simultaneous conversion of these distinct characteristics, offering numerous applications in fundamental studies and high-precision measurements. We illustrate our concept with two examples: the concurrent conversion of various waveforms, such as Gaussian and Bessel beams, into orthogonal polarization states; and the transformation of photonic quantum signals from one polarization state to another between distinct spectral frequencies.

This research delves into the electronic properties of DNA, focusing on how specific point mutations within the DNA strand affect electronic transport. Utilizing the nonequilibrium Green's function in the framework of nonequilibrium quantum transport, we investigate how these mutations influence electronic conduction. Our study concentrates on two distinct scenarios: (a) a mismatch occurring between two A bases, and (b) a mismatch occurring between two C bases. Notably, we discover that the electronic conduction properties differ significantly between these two cases, with scenario (a) exhibiting a decrease in conduction and scenario (b) exhibiting an increase. Moreover, we find that replacing an A with G and an A with T has a substantial impact on conduction, whereas replacing a C with G and C with T has a relatively minor effect. Our analysis also reveals that the electronic conduction of DNA, including mismatched regions, is significantly influenced by the surrounding environment, which can either enhance or hinder this transport depending on its electrical properties.

This paper tackles the challenge of accurately aligning multiple sets of points in a common space, even in the presence of noise. We draw inspiration from nature and work under a novel assumption that each set of points can be seen as a cluster of optimal starting positions. We combine a robust clustering algorithm with an optimization strategy, utilizing an underlying structure to simplify our approach and provide accurate results. We also incorporate a resilience test to ensure our method provides consistent solutions. We evaluate our algorithm using both simulated and real-world data sets and find it outperforms existing methods.

Our research focused on the magnetic properties of a polycrystalline sample composed of hexagonal-phase Tb3RuO7. Our findings indicate that the ground state of this sample is characterized by the coexistence of partially disordered and ordered states. These states are characterized by the formation of a spin-s = 1/2 state with an exchange coupling of approximately 1.7 K between neighboring Tb3RuO7 moments, as well as the formation of spin-s = 3/2 Ru multiple spin chains. The latter are unevenly modulated with a period of 3 and are subjected to a significant internal magnetic field induced by a strong anisotropy resulting from the close proximity of neighboring Tb3RuO7 moments. Our analysis suggests that the internal magnetic field is approximately 20 times stronger than the exchange coupling between neighboring spin chains. Consequently, the spin-3/2 state within the spin chains is significantly reduced by the action of the internal magnetic field. Our observations are consistent with the results of specific-heat and magnetization experiments.

This study aims to identify necessary and sufficient conditions for the optimality of various mathematical optimization problems involving DC functions. Specifically, we focus on the optimality of eigenvalue and trace problems for matrices with real entries, and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for a family of symmetric matrices to achieve optimality. Our research also extends to the optimality criteria of various mathematical programs with constraints, including mathematical programs with equilibrium constraints, semidefinite relaxations, and minimax optimization problems. Finally, we examine the optimality of general distance optimization problems and its connection to the generalized eigenvalue problem.

The mechanism behind the Higgs VEV's behavior in the Veneziano limit has the potential to be the key to understanding the qCD behavior at low energies, especially in terms of the IR cutoff. A non-Abelian SU(N_c) gauge theory is assumed to be the QCD analog of the D(-1)/D7 brane system. A key aspect of this system is the "dual string" that lives on the D7 brane, which has been found to be the analog of the "dual string" in QCD. A non-trivial dual string field does exist when the IR cutoff is much larger than the QCD scale, but it disappears as the IR cutoff decreases to a point much smaller than the QCD scale. A novel approach to studying QCD's behavior at low energies has been proposed, based on the idea that the dual string field's behavior can be understood as a signal of the string scale. A key aspect of this system is the "string tension", which has been found to play a crucial role in determining the IR cutoff. A further investigation into the D(-1)/D7 system has revealed that the string tension is analogous to the "dilaton" in the string tension, which has been found to be the analog of the "dilaton" in the string tension. A key aspect of this system is the "dilaton" profile, which has been found to be the analog of the "dilaton"

We're introducing a novel collision detection method that utilizes area overlap algorithms to confirm collisions between objects in 2D environments, which can be applied to various object shapes including intricate designs. This approach is particularly well-suited for environments featuring obstacles that have curved edges or sharp corners. The proposed method is being integrated within a existing pathfinding algorithm called Vector Field, which was previously outlined in January 2022 paper "Non-Uniform Vector Field, An Optimal Collision Handling Method for Path Finding".

We introduce a Bayesian framework that enhances deep reinforcement learning by
incorporating advanced knowledge from control theory. This approach, called
Bayesian Controller Integration, is a data-efficient method for robot control
that combines the strengths of Bayesian inference, deep reinforcement learning,
and modern robotics. Our framework is versatile and can be used to model a
wide range of control systems, from simple linear controllers to complex
non-linear neural networks. We have successfully tested Bayesian Controller
Integration on challenging manipulation tasks and achieved high success rates
while utilizing minimal data. Notably, we have demonstrated a threefold
improvement in sample efficiency compared to traditional deep reinforcement
learning, and have successfully integrated control theory by estimating the
parameters of a sophisticated Smith-Painlev\`e control system.

The exact mechanism behind stroke is not fully understood, making it difficult for clinicians to assess blood flow in the brain. A widely used method to evaluate stroke damage is through perfusion imaging, measuring the accumulation of tracer over time. A new approach to this imaging is presented, using a differentiable deconvolution to reduce noise and improve accuracy. When compared to traditional least squares deconvolution, the proposed method shows more consistent results in measuring brain damage and agreeing with clinical diagnoses.

We have computed the third order in QCD expansion for the ray function related to zero-jettiness, while leveraging the limit of collinear factorization to simplify the process. This calculation's complexity is significantly reduced by the presence of soft and collinear algebraic simplifications that allow us to transform the N$^3$LO cross-section cross-term into collinear counting. This transformation, combined with the use of a novel integral decomposition method, makes it possible to complete the third order QCD expansion for the zero-jettiness cross-section. The third order QCD expansion for the zero-jettiness cross-section has been computed up to the first term in collinear counting and the results are presented in both form and the most simplified form available.

This paper aims to explore chordal properties of power graphs, which was initially introduced in [J. Algebr. Comb. 2 (2002), page 35]. We will examine the chordality of power graphs of groups with limited exponents. To accomplish this, we must find a complete ordering for the power graph, which enables us to establish the edge ordering based on a corresponding ordering of vertices. We will begin by examining abelian groups and demonstrate that their power graphs are chordal. We will then consider non-abelian groups and observe that their power graphs are not necessarily chordal. To circumvent this issue, we will introduce the concept of edge-chordal graphs and demonstrate that the edge-chordal versions of power graphs are chordal. We will provide examples of edge-chordal groups and conclude by examining the chordality of dihedral and dicyclic groups.

In the complex scenario of target source separation, multiple signal sources are distorted by various systems and mixed together. The goal is to accurately reconstruct the original signals, which is a critical problem in target detection, as it requires obtaining clean signals for identification. This complex task is typically addressed through deep learning-based methods. Our research introduces a novel approach called optimal environment training, which enhances the performance of the model by creating an artificial environment where the signal sources are isolated. The clean signals are then used as the true labels in the training process, resulting in improved separation capabilities. By testing our method, known as OST-TSS, in target source separation tasks, we found that it can achieve a significant 4.8% increase in detection accuracy compared to conventional end-to-end training methods.

This study delves into the concept of coherence within the Quantum Information theory framework, specifically examining it through the lens of information theory observations in a universal quantum framework. Focusing on quantum coherence that is adaptable to different measurement bases, we begin by identifying it through the prism of information theory. We then derive semi-definite programming programs and optimize them to quantify coherence in relation to various quantum measurements, demonstrating the link between coherence and information theory observations. Our novel approach is proven effective by showcasing its capabilities in diagnosing coherence in various conditions, such as quantum channels and quantum-classical channels, and revealing unique properties of coherence.

A study of type C Quasi-periodic oscillations in several outbursts of the black hole X-ray binary H 1743--322 has been conducted using data from the Rossi X-ray satellite. The data analysis involved determining the power spectra of the source during the rising and declining phases of each outburst and identifying the characteristic frequencies of the type C QPOs. The results show that these frequencies vary systematically between outbursts, with a correlation between the characteristic frequencies and the hardness ratios of the source. The data were fit to a model that describes the accretion of gas onto the black hole, with the characteristic frequencies of the type C QPOs used as constraints. The results of the model fits suggest that the accretion of gas onto the black hole is likely to be in the form of a thin disk, with the mass flow rate increasing as the outburst reaches its peak. The results also suggest that the characteristic frequencies of the type C QPOs are likely to be determined by the accretion of gas onto the black hole, rather than by other factors.

The shift to digital governance, known as e-governance, has been facilitated by the widespread adoption of the HTTP/HTML platform. In contrast to previous government initiatives, which focused on print media, this new framework enables the creation and sharing of digital content, including information, services, and applications, using a scalable and maintainable approach. Our proposed system utilizes a standardized, modular framework that can be easily shared among employees, thus promoting collaboration and consistency across different governance initiatives. This platform, with its modular and component-based architecture, is designed to facilitate this sharing and has been successfully implemented using Python's Kombinator library.

Recent PANDA experiments have provided groundbreaking insights into the missing baryons, a long-standing mystery in physics that PANDA is specifically designed to tackle. This paper delves into the current state of research on these enigmatic particles, focusing on three key areas: the thorny issue of diquarks, the role of the continuum in scattering studies, and the continuum's influence on generalizing the partial wave analysis results to the continuum. Additionally, the paper touches on the continuum's impact on transition form factor analysis and the continuum's effect on measuring scattering parameters. Ultimately, the paper highlights the importance of accounting for the continuum in obtaining reliable results, and PANDA's unique capabilities in this regard.

The problem of exact left divider placement for trees and superstars has been extensively researched, and various algorithms have been developed to address this issue. A new problem is introduced - efficiently identifying all potential left dividers of a size 3 or less for trees with specific network structures. This problem is proven to be solvable within a polynomial time framework, and the proposed method is adaptable and can be applied to various tree types, such as those lacking the 2-leaf star edge or those that are cactus-like, both resulting in a polynomial time complexity solution.

We have analyzed a diverse range of galaxy evolution patterns in post-starburst and Balmer-strong galaxies, which are observed in the cores of these systems.  By examining galaxy cores with high stellar velocity dispersion, we found a distinct difference in their evolution paths compared to those with lower dispersion cores.  In particular, the cores with high stellar velocity dispersion tend to experience a faster cooling and contraction due to their higher gas content, which results in a different evolutionary path.  As a result, the transition of these cores from Balmer-strong to post-starburst stages occurs more rapidly, which is quantified by the time required to reach the post-starburst stage.  In contrast, the cores with lower stellar velocity dispersion show a slower cooling and contraction and therefore experience a longer transition period.  Additionally, the Balmer-strong cores with high stellar velocity dispersion tend to have a higher gas content compared to their post-starburst counterparts, which is attributed to the gas-rich nature of these galaxies.  Furthermore, the cores of Balmer-strong galaxies exhibit a higher gas content compared to post-starburst galaxies, which is consistent with the findings of previous studies.  In conclusion, the evolution paths of galaxy cores in post-starburst and Balmer-strong systems are influenced by their stellar mass and velocity dispersion.

In reconfigurable wireless networks, the proliferation of diverse radio interfaces and computing resources at the edge of the network enables the application of advanced techniques to optimize resource allocation. This research introduces a performer-critic learning scheduler that simultaneously allocates resources to the radio interfaces and edge computing nodes with the aim of optimizing a specific quality of service metric. The proposed approach combines a neural network-based learner with a reinforcement learning agent. The learner is trained offline to establish the relationship between resource allocation and quality of service, while the reinforcement learning agent dynamically allocates resources in real-time based on its estimates of the effects of different actions on the quality of service metric. The proposed approach is shown to improve quality of service through simulation in comparison to alternative methods.

Post-editing, particularly in the NLP domain, is an essential process where human experts correct flawed machine-generated outputs. To provide optimal guidance, a model should thoroughly understand both the errors in the machine-generated text and the principles governing fluent English. Prior approaches to measuring the comprehensiveness of language models in this context focus solely on individual words, but our research reveals that assessing terms (lexemes) as units of analysis can yield more accurate results and prove beneficial for post-editing support. Building upon the existing WordLevelQA framework, a new TermLevelQA system was developed, incorporating techniques such as lemmatization and the addition of a term-level attention mechanism to effectively capture term relationships. Experimental results demonstrate that TermLevelQA outperforms WordLevelQA in term-level quality assessment and offers potential benefits for post-editing tasks.

We investigate how dark stars' shadows, as seen from a distant observer, behave under specific conditions, namely when Kerr mass $m$ approaches a critical value $M_{\rm max}(r_0)$, which relies on the space-time's curvature radius $r_0$. This study aims to find a universal constant that links the critical mass with the spin of the dark star, which we call $M_{\rm max}(r_0)$ and $a$, respectively. Our research shows that the dark star's shadow is characterized by an inner edge and an outer edge, with the former depending solely on $M_{\rm max}(r_0)$ and the latter depending on both $M_{\rm max}(r_0)$ and $a$. We find that the ratio of the inner edge to the outer edge is approximately 0.525 for all cases, revealing a universal relationship. Furthermore, we establish that this ratio is independent of $r_0$ and solely dependent on $a$. We also find that the ratio of the outer edge to the spin-dependent shadow radius is a constant for all cases, with a value of approximately 2.217, which is independent of both $a$ and $r_0$.

This paper proposes a groundbreaking formulation of relativistic fluid dynamics in two-dimensional space, achieving a significant reduction in computational costs. By reorganizing key terms, the new formulation simplifies equation resolution and eliminates redundant calculations. As a result, the proposed enhanced formulation significantly outperforms its counterparts in terms of efficiency and accuracy. In support of its effectiveness, the paper includes a numerical example that highlights its benefits and a concise C++ code snippet demonstrating its implementation.

The BESIII detector equipped with the Helium target, operating at the BEPCII accelerator, collected data with a total luminosity of 2.0 fb^-1 at center-of-mass energies between 4.01 GeV and 4.6 GeV. To investigate the $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ meson decaying into $K^0_{\rm S} D^{*+}$ and $K^0_{\rm S} D^{*0}$, the data were analyzed using a two-dimensional distribution of the decay products of the $K^0_{\rm S}$ meson and the transverse momentum of the $D^{(*)+}$ meson. The analysis identified the $D^{* (2380) +}$ and $D^{* (2420 )+}$ mesons through their transitions to the $K^0_{\rm S} D^{*+}$ and $K^0_{\rm S} D^{*0}$ channels. The measured decay widths are $\Gamma_{D^{* (2380+) } \to K^0_{\rm S} D^{*+}} / \Gamma_{D^{* (2380+) } \to D^{*+}}$ and $\Gamma_{D^{* (2420 )+}} / \Gamma_{D^{* (2420 )+}}$, with corresponding values of 0.76 $\pm$ 0.

This study builds on previous work (Math Proc. Cam. Ser. Found. Comm. Mat. 83, 2003, arXiv:math.FA/0512415), focusing on a specific type of function, fractal polynomials, defined over the Sierpiński triangle. Key aspects of this research include examining fractal polynomials' continuity within the limit space of the Sierpiński triangle and deriving dimension-based estimates for sets where fractal polynomials are above or below a certain value.

In an exploratory study, we investigate visual inquiry design, an innovative method for generating data visualizations tailored to specific exploration tasks. Data visualizations are created through an iterative process involving a user who responds to prompts and creates visualizations to address an exploration task. Each created visualization serves as a source of insight, guiding the development of new questions and visualization requests. To facilitate this process, we've established a database containing 1,500+ diagrams from various domains and created an interactive tool that allows users to browse and refine their selections based on specific criteria. Using this resource, we've identified design patterns in data visualizations and informally identified key characteristics that influence the types of inquires they can answer. Building on this knowledge, we've developed an interactive system that enables users to browse diagrams and generate targeted visualizations designed to answer specific exploration questions.

The supernova-driven metal distribution model is based on the premise that supernovae diffuse the heavy elements within the halo, altering the density distribution. Research has suggested that this could explain the discrepancy between the shapes of the velocity and density profiles in some dwarf galaxies. This model has gained support from the discovery that metal-poor stars in the Milky Way's halo exhibit a density distribution that does not match the shape of the velocity distribution. However, the connection between the heavy elements and the distribution of the stars is still a topic of debate. To further investigate this phenomenon, we analyzed the data from the APOGEE-2 and LAMOST surveys to determine the relationship between the heavy elements and the distribution of the stars in the Milky Way's halo. Our results indicate that the distribution of the heavy elements follows the shape of the velocity distribution at low metal content, but follows the shape of the velocity-anisotropy profile at high metal content. This suggests that the supernova-driven model may not fully account for the displacement of the metal-poor stars in the Milky Way's halo. Our findings also show that the supernova-driven model does not explain the difference in the density distribution of the metal-poor stars in the Milky Way's halo compared to the Milky Way's globular clusters.

Higher-order logic is a robust foundation for software verification that can be expressed through higher-order logic model checking, although its use is typically hindered by the undecidability of standard inferences within this system. One effective approach to overcome this limitation is to employ an extraction strategy that transforms higher-order logic model checking into the more efficient first-order logic propositional calculus, specifically the propositional calculus with the ability to use unbound variables. Our research aims to improve the understanding of extraction methods and develop new techniques for transforming higher-order logic model checking into first-order logic propositional calculus, specifically in the context of sat. A key challenge in this area is developing an understanding of the properties required for the extraction function to be compatible with sat. We have identified necessary and sufficient conditions for the extraction function to be sat-checking correct and have developed a procedure to apply these conditions to establish new extraction theorems. One notable application of our research is the derivation of new saturation theorems for the first-order calculus with the ability to use unbound variables, including saturation theorems that facilitate model construction and proof construction.

A solution to the Tartaria hypothesis for ancient writing requires demonstrating the possibility of discovering similar ordering patterns in ancient cultures and proposed methods for replicating the Tartaria script with minimal information about its rules. A transformation of the 26-letter Latin alphabet into a binary system is used, representing each character by two characteristics: similarity in sound and shape. Characteristic functions measure how well individual characters match ideal representations of their corresponding sound and shape features. Rules governing character evolution are defined as transformations that preserve the similarity characteristics. By applying these rules repeatedly, a dynamic system is created, and computer simulations show that certain initial character configurations can generate stable patterns resembling the Tartaria script, thereby supporting the plausibility of the hypothesized rules with minimal parameter adjustment.

We develop a method based on the empirical risk minimization principle to derive the theoretical framework for the random forest algorithm. Our approach enables the derivation of finite-sample and large-sample properties for the algorithm's output, effectively extending the applicability of the standard U-statistic theory to the adapted random forest framework. In addition, we establish a normal approximation framework for U-statistics with kernel functions that depend on a parameter, which facilitates the derivation of asymptotic normality for the random forest estimator of the regression coefficient.

A novel approach to solving a complex optimization problem arising from the electric vehicle charging problem in a distributed context is proposed. Due to the incompatibility of the electric vehicles' (EVs) power constraints with the power grid's voltage constraints, a hierarchical network structure is utilized. In this setup, the grid controller and EVs are considered as separate layers with varying communication capabilities. An efficient algorithm, based on the modified Communication-Restricted-ADMM framework, along with a theoretical convergence analysis, is developed to address the optimization issue. Additionally, a method to adjust the local cost is introduced to achieve better performance. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods in terms of both convergence speed and grid power quality.

To study the electronic properties and structural stability of $SmFeO_3$, the density functional method is employed. Perovskite samples of $SmFeO_3$ with hexagonal and rhombohedral structures are investigated through the application of density functional theory using the plane wave pseudopotential method. Results reveal that both bulk and low-energy 2D nanosheets have hexagonal structures, while bulk and low-energy 2D nanosheets with a rhombohedral structure are found to be stable. This contrasts with previous research suggesting the rhombohedral structure of the bulk as unstable. Furthermore, the study confirms that the electronic properties and elastic constants of $SmFeO_3$ with a hexagonal structure are superior to those with a rhombohedral structure.

The human microbiome plays a vital part in the body's functioning; even slight alterations can lead to diseases. To address diseases, it's crucial to understand how the microbiome operates. However, studying this complex system is challenging. To gain insight into its workings, researchers need to explore the vast space of possible combinations of metabolic reactions. This uncharted territory is known as the microbiome phenotype network. Our study proposes a novel approach to charting this network by utilizing a computational algorithm. This algorithm efficiently maps the vast space of possible combinations of metabolic reactions. Our results show that the microbiome phenotype network has distinct small clusters of interconnected reactions, indicating a hierarchical structure. This hierarchical structure is influenced by the unique metabolic capabilities of the bacteria present. Our study demonstrates that this network can be used to predict the impact of specific antibiotics on the human microbiome. By mapping the vast space of possible combinations of metabolic reactions, researchers can better comprehend the complex relationships within the human microbiome. This knowledge can inform the development of effective treatments for diseases.

A data-driven approach to building ventilation is proposed. This approach includes developing a model to forecast ventilation quality, a control model to adjust control signals, and a reinforcement learning agent to make optimal adjustments. The reinforcement learning agent uses a double deep Q-learning algorithm and can adapt to changing conditions within a building. Experimental results show that this data-driven method outperforms traditional methods in reducing energy consumption while maintaining acceptable indoor air quality.

We have thoroughly investigated the supernova (SN) 2017gci, a spectacular transient event that was classified as a superluminous supernova type I. By analyzing the SN's characteristics and the host galaxy's redshift, we determined that SN 2017gci is likely a pair of merging stars with a total mass of approximately 15 solar masses, consisting of a primary star with 30 solar masses of hydrogen and a secondary star with 8 solar masses. The larger star in this binary system is likely a blue supergiant, and the smaller star is likely a Wolf-Rayet star. Our findings suggest that SN 2017gci is likely a result of the collapse of a massive star that has experienced significant mass loss and has been powered by the helium-rich core. The large, bright light curve of SN 2017gci is similar to that of the V-band light curve of the SN 2008es, and the SN's characteristics are likely a result of the interaction between the SN's ejecta and the circumstellar medium. Our analysis indicates that the SN 2017gci system is likely a result of the inspiral of the two stars, and the SN's characteristics are likely a result of the SN's ejecta interacting with the circumstellar medium.

Researchers have introduced a quantum version of the well-known Stoner-Wohlfarth model for magnets with two-dimensional arrangements of solitary magnetic particles connected through spin interaction in the z-direction. The expanded model accounts for both the magnetocrystalline anisotropy and the quantum process of a single spin flip occurring within the z-axis, resulting in an energy transition that is influenced by the particle's z-moment and the distance between particles. The model's predictions align with both the classical and quantum theories, particularly in their rotation dynamics, as the energy of rotation is preserved in the system. The model's applicability is further supported by the investigation of the magnetic properties of graphene-based systems, where it was found that the magnetization direction of graphene-based nanostructures can be controlled using a specific type of magnetic field known as the spin-polarized Landau-Zener-Ginzburg-Landau field.

A technique for producing dependencies in the Dependency Quadruple Format has been developed, which combines the best of two prominent approaches: one utilizing a neural-based partial parser and the other incorporating a visual attention mechanism inspired by biology. When tested on the Conll 12 dataset, this method demonstrated superior performance compared to previous approaches, achieving an accurate dependency parsing rate of 90.81% (LAS).

The task of automatic image prediction, a binary classification problem, aims to determine whether an input image contains a picture. In this context, we explore the application of feature contribution techniques to address this challenge, and we discuss the implications of using such methods for this specific task. To this end, we conducted a thorough analysis of the effects of varying the number of retained sub-samples on the performance of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model, and we compared the performance of the CNN model with its counterpart that has been regularized using the feature contribution technique.

We investigate the linear stability of a thin-shell wormhole model with a reflection-asymmetry property, which exhibits dual images in the shadow region. This model, first introduced in a 2022 paper, features two wormholes that exist independently and only shares a finite surface segment. Our analysis focuses on the stability of this setup under radial pressure variations and a general fluid distribution, and we find that it remains stable when a certain condition related to the wormholes' shadow angles is met. Interestingly, this criterion is independent of the distance between the wormholes. Additionally, our study examines the impact of a radial pressure gradient on this stability, and we find that increasing this gradient may render the wormholes unstable.

We examine the expected value of a maximum interval without a point of interest in a sequence of random steps, as well as its relationship to the expected area covered by a random path in two-dimensional space. Our study reveals that these expectations are significantly influenced by the structure of the underlying point set and space geometry. In particular, we derive inequalities for the expected values of maximum intervals and covered areas in various scenarios, such as unit discs and regular polygons, and arrange them in a specific order. These inequalities imply that the expected values decrease as the point set or space order increases. Moreover, we establish that in a particular scenario of equally spaced points in a circle, the expected values of maximum intervals and covered areas coincide with those of a random path in a particular arrangement of the unit line segment.

Recent research on the triangular lattice has revealed that trimer shields play a significant role in the quantum critical properties of the model.  This particular interaction between nearest-neighbor clusters, which is difficult to observe experimentally due to its density, is crucial in determining the behavior of the model.  Trimmer shields exhibit non-trivial properties that distinct from other nearest-neighbor interactions; they are pivotal in understanding the physics of the corresponding model.  This review provides a comprehensive overview of the trimer shield, its connection to the quantum critical properties of the model, and related topics that require further research and clarification.

Recent advances in deep learning have led to the development of numerous image classification datasets, each with its unique distribution of classes. This has given rise to the universal domain adaptation challenge, where a single, universally applicable classifier is sought that can be trained on multiple datasets with distinct class distributions without needing to first match these distributions in a shared feature space. This paper proposes a novel Universal Domain Adjustment (UDA) framework that addresses this challenge by learning two types of relationships: between prototypes within and across classes in different domains, based on their mutual points. This enables the classifier to accurately estimate probabilities for each class in any domain, even when class distributions differ. We demonstrate the effectiveness of UDA through experiments on various datasets, including MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and the large-scale ImageNet dataset.

This paper introduces a method for 3D model reconstruction of automobiles from stereo images, incorporating a specific type of shape guidance that's tailored to individual car models. This shape guidance is represented by a 3D model of a car's body, comprising a geometric representation of a car's planar components and curved surfaces. The proposed technique leverages a subcategory-aware shape guidance approach, which enhances the overall reconstruction quality. A novel pose evaluation metric is also developed to evaluate the accuracy of 3D model pose predictions before the reconstruction process, leading to improved results on the KITTI stereo dataset with a 7% reduction in reconstruction error. Experimental evaluations using this dataset demonstrate that the new approach yields more accurate 3D reconstruction outcomes.

Advanced methods for answering complex questions through knowledge graphs have been developed, incorporating not only the meaning of individual words, but also how the words within a question are connected to the underlying knowledge graph. Current approaches to this task typically use a pipeline-based system where a parser first breaks down the question into its component parts before a reasoner identifies the required information. However, this sequential process can be inefficient, particularly when the question contains multiple questions or requires specific domain knowledge. To address these limitations, we propose a new approach that allows the question graph to be modified in a step-by-step manner. Our approach involves creating an outline of the question graph by selecting relevant parts of the knowledge graph and then filling in the missing information to provide the required answers. Experiments have shown that our method performs significantly better than previous approaches, achieving an improvement of 7.3% in accuracy for a variety of question types.

This work explores the interplay between polynomial combinations and monoid spaces, 
exposing their commonalities and distinct features. We delve into the algebraic 
framework of polynomial combinations, highlighting its unique properties, and relate 
it to graded commutative algebras. We also investigate the category of monoid spaces, 
revealing its similarities and differences to the category of polynomial combinations. 
Ultimately, we outline potential applications of these frameworks in algebraic 
generalizations and computations.

Stream-based data is becoming increasingly prevalent, and is expected to be generated by a wide variety of sources in the near future. The extraction of meaningful entities from this stream-based data is essential for uncovering hidden relationships, identifying key interactions, and for instance, detecting money laundering. Our research involves investigating the application of Named Entity Resolution to stream-based data, a complex task that requires the accurate identification and reconciliation of variations in entity representations within and across data streams. Building on the popular Graphscope platform for processing streaming graphs, we have developed a comprehensive library of entity resolution algorithms and a benchmarking framework that can be used to compare their effectiveness. Our experiments, conducted using synthetic and real-world datasets, have shown that a simple yet efficient merge-SG algorithm outperforms more advanced techniques such as interleave-SG, window-based SG, and coarsening filter algorithms in terms of processing speed and accuracy. Our results also highlight the importance of data characteristics in determining the chosen entity resolution algorithm, as different techniques excel in specific scenarios.

In the context of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, the oblique adjustments 
$S$, $T$, and $U$ are typically estimated using the one-loop effective Lagrangian
in the presence of Higgs sector gauge interactions, which involves a single top quark 
loop contributing to $S$ and $T$, and two top quark loops contributing to $U$. 
However, this approach is based on a simplified expansion of the Higgs sector, which 
includes only the lightest Higgs as a distinct component. 
In this work, we investigate the impact of a more comprehensive Higgs sector, 
which comprises three distinct Higgs bosons, namely $H_1$, $H_2$, and $H_3$. 
We derive the one-loop effective Lagrangian for $S$, $T$, and $U$ in this 
extended Higgs sector, and identify the key factors influencing our results. 
We specifically examine the influence of the lightest $H_2$-like scalar on $S$, 
$T$, and $U$, which can be interpreted as the effect of an additional vector boson 
in the $S$ and $U$ observables.

We introduce a novel approach that generates 360-degree perspectives from dynamic video clips without relying on pre-defined camera paths or motion control. This method transforms dynamic footage into a 360-degree perspective framework, enabling the creation of immersive 360-degree experiences from monocular inputs. Our technique has broad applications, particularly in the entertainment sector, where it can produce realistic 360-degree content from single-camera footage, and in education, where it can facilitate access to 360-degree content for those without specialized equipment. This method is also adaptable to various formats, including virtual reality, augmented reality, and 360-degree streaming, and it can be applied to real-time dynamic scenes without time constraints.

The study explores the behavior of the solutions to the given differential equation under the assumption that the initial displacement is very large, which leads to the solutions deviating significantly from the gradient of the potential over time. Specifically, it examines whether and how far the solutions drift away from the potential gradient within a specified time frame when the initial displacement exceeds a certain threshold, denoted by the symbol $\epsilon$. 

For scenarios where the potential is bounded from below, it has been proven that the solutions remain bounded from below and above, and that the difference between the second derivative and the derivative of the potential remains bounded from below and can be arbitrarily negative. 

For scenarios where the potential is bounded from below and exhibits convexity, it has been proven that the solutions remain bounded from below and that the difference between the second derivative and the potential remains bounded from below and can be arbitrarily negative. 

For scenarios where the potential is bounded from below but is not convex, it has been proven that the solutions remain bounded from below and that the difference between the second derivative and the potential remains bounded from below and can be arbitrarily negative.

A random grain model, defined by the sum of discrete, time-invariant Dirac functions, is used to model a nonlinear system, where the system's behavior is analyzed using scaling analysis. This analysis reveals that the system's scaling properties depend on the specific model parameters, with distinct regions exhibiting unique scaling behavior. Specifically, the system exhibits a diffusion scaling in one region, while an anti-diffusion scaling in another region, with a unique critical behavior separating these two regions. This critical behavior is characterized by the scaling of a logarithmic function. Our findings are verified through numerical simulations of the nonlinear system, specifically Burgers' equation, under various initial conditions.

Recent breakthroughs in intelligent surfaces technology have led to significant
advances in 6G wireless communications, positioning it for widespread adoption.
This study delves into the realm of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces in
6G, examining their applications, benefits, and regulatory challenges. A
comprehensive overview of their design considerations, such as RF hardware and
algorithmic requirements, is also provided. Furthermore, the study explores
the evolving policy landscape and technical standards applicable to this new
technology. Lastly, the study identifies potential research avenues to
facilitate practical implementation of intelligent surfaces in future
communications networks.

This paper introduces a method for simplifying complex probabilistic multi-agent systems, specifically those with stable regions and multiple equilibrium states. By leveraging information on agent positions, the proposed approach enhances the stability assessment of system configurations and streamlines computational requirements for analyzing probabilistic multi-agent systems, as evidenced by numerical studies on the Chelyabinsk rockery and the Bak-Takagi active particle system.

Recent years have seen an increase in the use of quantization to reduce the memory requirements of Deep Neural Networks, allowing them to run directly on hardware without the need for advanced computational tools. Most existing methods for quantization involve a two-stage approach where a pre-trained network is fine-tuned using a full floating-point representation, followed by a quantization process in the second stage. This approach has been successful in practice, but it has several limitations that can impact performance, including the potential for the first stage to "overfit" and destroy the balance between representation capacity and computation power, and the fact that it relies on a single "global" threshold to make predictions about the quality of the quantization process. This paper proposes a new approach called Cyclic Training and Multiple Quantization, where the training process is split into multiple stages, each involving a combination of quantization and fine-tuning, and where the quality of the quantization process is evaluated using a series of local thresholds that are applied at the end of each stage. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by applying it to a variety of popular vision models, including MobileNet and VGG, and show that it yields significant improvements in performance, including a 1.5% increase in the Top-1 accuracy of the MobileNet model on the ImageNet dataset when using only 8 bits for both weights and activations.

The core-degenerate (CD) pathway for type Ia supernovae formation is plausible and consistent with observational data. However, the core-degenerate scenario requires the merger of two white dwarf stars with nearly equal mass. This paper investigates the characteristics of double-degenerate binaries leading to a 1.2 solar mass progenitor star core-degenerate explosion outcome. The study found that a 1.2 solar mass white dwarf merger occurs when two 1.2 solar mass stars initially merge to form a 1.2 solar mass white dwarf. The 1.2 solar mass white dwarf then undergoes a helium core ignition, resulting in a helium white dwarf merger. The white dwarf merger process is found to be more likely to occur in the range of 0.5 to 1.5 solar mass white dwarfs. The study found that 1.2 solar mass white dwarf mergers are typically the result of 0.9 to 1.2 solar mass white dwarf mergers. The study found that 1.2 solar mass white dwarf mergers are primarily composed of 0.5 to 0.7 solar mass white dwarf material and 0.5 to 0.7 solar mass helium white dwarf material. The study found that 1.2 solar mass white dwarf mergers exhibit a red supergiant-like luminosity of 10,000 solar luminosities and a temperature of 10,000 Kelvin, similar to 19- and

A primary educational goal is to develop students' ability to think critically, solve complex problems, and apply theoretical knowledge to real-world issues. This paper explores strategies for enhancing students' capabilities in critical thinking, problem-solving, and practical application. We present a proven framework for a massive open online course on advanced topics, encompassing subfields of machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and software engineering. This course is designed to enable students to tackle various real-world challenges. Furthermore, we outline a general approach to creating educational resources with associated critical thinking and problem-solving exercises. We utilize this approach to develop a collection of resources in machine learning, allowing students to develop and apply algorithms for various real-world scenarios.

A novel COVID-19 vaccine has been developed, offering hope for an end to the pandemic. Despite its promise, vaccination efforts face significant obstacles, including the manual tracking of immunization, scammers, and technology limitations. We propose an innovative blockchain-based solution to streamline immunization registration and tracking, ensuring the success of vaccination programs worldwide. Our approach, suited for low-power devices, leverages blockchain technology to securely record and verify immunization data, maintaining data integrity even across different platforms. The proposed architecture incorporates a lightweight blockchain and smart contract, enabling seamless vaccination status verification across various data formats and systems. The performance of our solution is demonstrated using two popular blockchain implementations, showing its adaptability across various environments. The outcome of our effort will significantly contribute to global public health by enhancing vaccination program effectiveness.

Recent advancements in educational technology have led to an influx of diverse resources designed to enhance student outcomes, primarily through online learning platforms. The primary goal of these resources is to decrease the workload of instructors and offer students increased access to high-quality educational materials. Yet, the effectiveness of these resources heavily depends on how they are integrated into the learning experience. A common approach to implementing this involves providing students with recommendations based on the resources they have accessed, with the aim of optimizing learning outcomes. The majority of current recommendation methods, however, are centered on the learner's profile rather than course attributes. Consequently, little is known about the relationships between courses from a practical standpoint. This paper investigates this knowledge gap, focusing on a specific university's course catalog. We develop a straightforward and robust method for recommending courses to students, which is underpinned by an explicit model of course clusters. Additionally, we examine the relationship between course recommendations and the explicit cluster model.

Our research shows that the breaking of particle-antiparticle symmetry can cause a localized quantum state to emerge even without an external potential. This breaking of symmetry creates a perfect, zero-range potential that attracts antiparticles, resulting in the formation of localized states. Furthermore, our findings indicate that the intensity of this interaction is significantly greater than previously thought, leading to the formation of highly localized "bright" soliton-like particles. This discovery opens up new possibilities for particle engineering and novel interactions, and may even lead to the development of new particles in high-energy experiments.

A quasiparticle known as a spin-wave, created by a highly correlated electron plasma, can be identified as a quasiparticle. The formation of these quasiparticles is a result of the combination of Coulomb and spin-rotation interactions. The presence of spin-rotation interactions results in a spin-charge coupled mode within the plasma, while Coulomb interactions are responsible for generating a charge-charge coupled mode. The study of the damping of these quasiparticles is conducted, and it is found that the influence of the spin-rotation and Coulomb interactions on these quasiparticles varies depending on their respective properties.

We've discovered a unique conformal field property in a Floquet system that exhibits behavior similar to well-known topological insulators. By using a simple and smooth control method, we can control the system to exhibit properties similar to conformal field theory with a central charge of 1. Our research shows that this is a stable state that remains even after small changes in the controlling signal. Importantly, this characteristic field is a natural outcome of our approach, and it doesn't rely on assumptions about the underlying microscopic processes.

A comprehensive deep learning framework is introduced for integrating data from multiple sensors, where each input consists of a combination of raw data and hidden representations derived from other inputs. This innovative approach enables models to leverage the hidden representations of one input as features for predicting tasks associated with another input. We demonstrate that this framework effectively handles the transfer of information between different sensors, allowing for the improvement of hidden representations. We apply this framework to a scenario involving proximity and infrared sensors in autonomous parking, utilizing the infrared sensor's hidden representations to inform estimates from the proximity sensor. We also examine the challenges of learning transferable representations and provide a method to capture these representations through the extraction of shared latent spaces between different sensors, both within the same time step or across time steps. Experimental results on a dataset of infrared and proximity sensors from the autonomous parking domain show that our proposed approach significantly outperforms baseline methods.

This study assesses the feasibility of measuring $\phi_s$ and $\Delta\gamma_s$ at LHCb through direct and indirect methods, including a new indirect approach that involves determining the $CP$ violation parameter of a certain charmless process using measurements from another related process. The direct methods involve analyzing time-dependent $D^0$ oscillations, while the indirect methods involve studying $CP$ violation in the decay of charged $D^+\to K^+ \pi^0$ through the decay of a related multibody decay. The study shows that future data from LHCb will allow for precise measurements of $\phi_s$ and $\Delta\gamma_s$ along with a new indirect measurement of $\phi_s$ based on the $CP$ violation in the decay of $D^0\to \eta h^+ h^-$.

In the field of secure communication, private message encoding is essential for maintaining secrecy.  Graph devices can be used to create secure messages by splitting data and routing it through a network, but this approach can be complex due to the need for extensive computation, storage, and coordination.  This paper presents a new framework that enables secure message transmission through a network, breaking it down into smaller components and providing more efficient solutions for a subset of "simple" networks, where individual nodes only perform basic operations and do not store full data distributions.

We developed an algorithm for networks with 3 nodes, showing it guarantees secure transmission of a message and its reverse, by eliminating potential eavesdropping scenarios.  Additionally, we developed an algorithm for networks with 4 nodes, with specific patterns of connectivity, that securely transmits a message among any 2 nodes out of a total of 3 possible senders, with the remaining node unable to eavesdrop.

This paper tackles the challenge of tracking labeled random finite sets in a multi-sensor environment.  To achieve this, a novel origin sampler is introduced that combines a dynamic model with sensor-specific observations.  This origin sampler is then used within a multi-sensor framework incorporating a joint probabilistic data association filter and cardinality robust probability hypothesis density filter to estimate the system state.  Specifically, the origin sampler's ability to utilize the combined data from multiple sensors improves target detection and classification, while its reduced computational cost allows for real-time estimation.  Through theoretical analysis and demonstrated in simulation, the proposed approach is shown to outperform the traditional single-sensor origin sampler in terms of target detection and classification performance.

Forecasts of language development over the next century are crucial for
understanding how languages might evolve in response to future challenges
and making informed decisions about which languages to support with technology.
To provide accurate forecasts, we need robust data models that can
account for the complex relationships between languages. This study aims to
create a data-driven framework for language attribute forecasting by analyzing
existing typological data and using it to train a machine learning model
that can make detailed, granular forecasts based on the language characteristics
of languages with available data. Since our goal is to make forecasts for
unobserved languages, we use a combination of data from observed languages
and their analogous counterparts in a novel, unsupervised approach that
involves ranking languages according to their similarity to a given target
language. We have developed a web-based platform that allows users to
access our forecasting tool, as well as the data and methods used to train
the model. This platform is available for on-line evaluation and will be
feature on the SIGTYP 2020 shared task website. Further details about
our forecasting approach and language data can be found in our accompanying
paper, which includes a step-by-step guide to forecasting language
discontinuities using our model and data.

In reinforcement learning, particularly in settings that demand learning from pre-existing environments, off-policy evaluation is crucial for assessing policy performance. This technique, which surpasses baseline methods by a significant margin, involves using a dataset recorded under an environment's baseline policy to evaluate a new, potentially superior policy. Despite its importance, off-policy evaluation often lacks comprehensive testing in real-world settings. This paper addresses this gap by conducting an extensive study on off-policy evaluation in a variety of real-world scenarios, including both simple and complex cases. Through this research, it is revealed that current methods experience declining accuracy as they tackle more complex tasks. Building on this finding, this study presents a new approach to off-policy evaluation, which surpasses existing methods in multiple real-world applications.
