Additionally, the work establishes a new relationship between the essential norms of $T_f$ and the original symbol $f$.

This study introduces a new influence measure for Bayesian analysis by combining measurement error theory and Galilean perturbation, which is a foundational element of robust statistics. By introducing a concept similar to the derivative of a probability density function, the paper proposes a sequence of influence measures that decrease over time, which is demonstrated within the framework of the Bernoulli-Categorical distribution.

In real-world applications, maintaining accurate anomaly detection is a significant challenge for audio systems, particularly when sensors malfunction or fail, leading to unrecognizable audio signals. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on extensive training datasets and may not adapt well to domain shifts. This research investigates a novel unsupervised anomaly detection approach, utilizing UMAP dimensionality reduction in conjunction with auto-correlation features from the DeepMind at Imperial College of London's Audio Set dataset. The results indicate that UMAP effectively visualizes complex audio data and highlight the efficacy of the auto-correlation feature in achieving high detection accuracy.

A theoretical analysis of two-component spin-1/2 fermions in the SU(N) model reveals a previously unknown type of ferromagnetism, characterized by a non-equilibrium state where magnetization can freely move through the system without cost. This phenomenon, known as nomadic ferromagnetism, is identified within a previously defined phase diagram originally classifying the system's equilibrium states. Furthermore, it is shown that this new state emerges from the Haldane phase when the system's spin-orbit interaction reaches a critical threshold. Nomadic ferromagnetism is distinguished from other known states by its lack of spontaneous symmetry, but research has yet to pinpoint the exact critical interaction value at which this state forms.

To study gamma-ray pulsars, we utilized a pre-trained neural network model called SNR-Bayes, which identifies new gamma-ray pulsars. SNB-Bayes was trained on a dataset consisting of Fermi LAT-detected gamma-ray pulsars. We then analyzed the Pulsar Catalog, which led us to discover 24 new pulsars. As a result, we increased our known gamma-ray pulsors by 14.2% and introduced 24 new pulsors. Our research further led to the categorization of pulsors into three distinct groups: pulsors resembling young pulsors at the stage of supernova remnant, pulsors that have undergone supernovae with a long period of time, and newly discovered pulsors.

In the realm of two-dimensional superfluids, a specific type of excitation called a magnetoroton is characterized by its spatially homogeneous and spin-polarized nature. We have discovered that magnetotorons dominate the low-frequency power spectrum in fractional quantum Hall systems at temperatures significantly higher than their energy gap. As temperature decreases, these torons give way to collective excitations influenced by the energy gap. Our research reveals that, in such quantum Hall systems, thermal fluctuations exhibit a unique type of spectral regulation known as total regulation. Notably, this regulation is distinct from the more conventional critical-state regulation associated with superconductors. Our findings suggest that, in fractional quantum Hall systems, thermal fluctuations exhibit universal spectral regulation behavior, regardless of their ground state properties.

The Energetic particles, x-rays, nucleonic, gamma-ray, ultrarelativistic particles (ENE) experiment is designed to study the gamma radiation produced by interactions between high-energy particles and the nucleus of atmospheric gases. It consists of three complementary telescopes: a small telescope measuring energy up to 40 GeV, a medium-sized telescope measuring up to 700 GeV, and a large telescope measuring up to 100 GeV. This paper describes the performance characteristics of the ENE telescopes.

The Cauchy problem for the truncated Boltzmann equation poses a significant challenge due to its highly singular, non-local nature, which emerges when $f$ approaches or falls below zero. This paper aims to resolve the issue with only minimal initial data, revealing a significant finding that the solution exhibits regularity comparable to that of the full Boltzmann equation under similar conditions.

Classifiers trained with noisy labels can produce inaccurate results due to biased learning.  To counteract this issue, we can leverage robust models capable of withering away when encountering erroneous training data.  A revised variant of the robust traceability matrix has been devised along with enhanced loss functions to facilitate the development of resilient classifiers.  Furthermore, robustness in the presence of noisy labels can also arise from classifiers' inherent biases.  A collection called FEMORAX, comprising 91 datasets across 20 domains, has been compiled to investigate the resilience of classifiers.  Notably, the FEMORAX dataset exhibits a notable disparity in the resilience of various classifiers, specifically GroupDrop and Decoupling, indicating that the FEMORAX dataset offers a valuable resource for identifying robustness mechanisms in classifiers.

This research focuses on a class of orbit codes, particularly those generated by cyclically permuted circular shifts, 
characterized by having automorphism groups that are isomorphic to a cyclic group. We develop a method for determining 
the group of automorphisms and the corresponding homomorphism for each self-orthogonal orbit code, and we derive 
a strategy to construct self-orthogonal orbit codes with high automorphism groups and large minimum distances. Furthermore, 
we introduce and analyze several types of symmetries inherent in orbit codes, classify these symmetries, and provide examples 
of orbit codes exhibiting various forms of symmetry.

A star in the ancient open cluster M67 has been identified as a potential benchmark for aging low-mass stars. Using the K2 space telescope, a precise mass measurement was obtained for this star by combining photometric data from the cluster with a parallax value from Gaia EDR3. The resulting mass value of 1.32 plus/minus 0.02 solar masses matches expectations from stellar evolution models. Notably, this high level of accuracy is comparable to that of the exoplanet-host star, which allows researchers to more accurately determine the age of the cluster. The age of M67 was then calculated by analyzing the color-magnitude diagram of the cluster, using the luminosity of the identified benchmark star. The resulting ages of 6.02 billion years and 6.5 billion years from the two benchmark stars are consistent with other estimates, and suggest that this benchmark star can be used to precisely determine the age of low-mass stars.

We establish a sufficient condition for the integral mean of the function $f^2(x)$, specifically that it must be less than or equal to $2$ for all $x$ in the interval $[0,1]$ and the function $f$ is an eigenfunction of the complex Schrödinger operator $\mathscr{L}_c = -d^2/dx^2+cx^\alpha$, where $\alpha$ is a positive value. This leads to a direct derivation of a well-known inequality: $|f(1)/f(0)|^2-\text{E}_{f}(1)=\int_{0}^{1}f^2(x)dx<2$. Furthermore, we show that the maximum of the function $|f|^2$ on the interval $[0,1]$ can also be bounded by one.

A critical aspect of SPH's success hinges on properly implementing the continuity equation, necessitating innovative methods for accurately representing gradients within the model. Building upon the multi-dimensional model developed by Thakur, Kleiser, and Sorensen, a new gradient estimation technique is proposed that leverages the SPH neighbors and an enhanced partition of unity. This approach involves introducing a variable that accounts for the extent of each point's influence, defined as the sum of squared weights associated with neighboring particles. By incorporating this influence variable (or its square root) into the gradient calculation, the resulting gradients are not only more accurate but also conserved, providing a robust foundation for SPH codes. To further improve the multi-dimensional gradient formula, a correction factor is introduced to mitigate the impact of points with negligible influence. This correction, applied as a multiplier, ensures the stability of the estimation technique even in the absence of significant gradients. By combining this correction with the influence variable, the resulting gradient formula is not only accurate but also conservative, providing a reliable basis for a wide range of SPH applications. To demonstrate the efficacy of this new approach, several test cases are presented that showcase its ability to produce accurate and consistent results, even in the presence of complex fluid interactions.

Capturing the full potential of spectral images involves combining the high contrast of bright pixels with the detailed spectral information of sensitive pixels. Current methods using pixel-wise or spectral map weights often sacrifice one aspect for another, but unfortunately, direct generation of pixel contrast with spectral information is a challenging task that previous spectral image reconstruction methods have struggled with. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel method called the Spectral Super-Enhancement Network with deep function-blending, which involves a single end-to-end training process. By defining contrast and detail as two separate functions of image pixels, we use a deep neural network to estimate these functions and map them to spectral images. We evaluate our method on various datasets, which shows that it outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in both quantitative and visual assessments.

In computer vision, accurately pinpointing the location of objects within geotagged images is a significant yet complex issue. To address this, our research introduces an innovative approach that considers the environment when localizing objects. This technique, known as context sensitive object geotagging (CSOG), utilizes a neural network that combines image and text inputs to predict object locations. Leveraging the Google Open Images dataset, CSOG demonstrates the capability to learn contextual dependencies between objects and its surroundings, ultimately producing more accurate geotags. Our experiments confirm that CSOG outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving notable improvements of 3.4% and 1.4% for class-wise and instance-wise geotagging respectively. Moreover, CSOG exhibits enhanced interpretability through the production of more accurate geotags.

Dam safety issues have been a significant global concern, and the link between dams and earthquakes has been a pressing problem in various countries. Many dams are constructed without detailed information on their construction methods, which can make it difficult to assess their stability. Following significant seismic events, dams tend to accumulate a large amount of sediment, posing a significant risk to the environment. In areas prone to drought, dam capacity is used to mitigate the issue. However, the construction of new dams in recent years has been primarily focused on providing clean water and preventing flooding. This research presents a novel approach to automatically detect and quantify dam storage depletion from satellite imagery using a customized metric-based system. The results of our study suggest that machine learning models can be effectively trained to recognize changes in dam storage levels by utilizing a metric that captures the relative difference in satellite imagery between dam and non-dam sites.

In 1983, Akhalaq et al. discovered a phenomenon called quantum flux suspension, which occurs when there is a sudden dynamic change in the motion of charged particles within a quantum system. This phenomenon, also known as QFZ, leads to the formation of quantum flux tubes that enable charged particles to move at speeds exceeding that of light. This paper proposes a new concept, the QFS-zone, which describes a region where a quantum flux tube dominates the motion of charged particles. Within a QFS-zone, both space and time can be measured in terms of their equivalent length, which is a function of the fundamental space-time constant. This phenomenon offers a theoretical explanation for the phenomenon of super-luminonization and provides insights into the nature of space and time.

Online shopping has significantly grown in popularity, resulting in a surge of data from product descriptions and images. Despite this, there's a pressing need to understand how consumers perceive and interact with products. This study focuses on predicting the Point-of-Attachment, a critical attribute that determines product interaction. From a data perspective, different products vary significantly, with some featuring lengthy, detailed descriptions while others rely solely on images. To address this, we've developed a novel hybrid approach that combines text and image data to classify Point-of-Attachment. We've also conducted experiments to understand how text and image features influence the model's performance.

The web has significantly expanded the scope for sharing information to the public, with social and financial markets being heavily influenced by it. Given the substantial economic implications, there's a pressing need to thoroughly examine the impact of cross-border digital information on financial markets. This research delves into the relationship between social activity and share price movements using a large-scale dataset of stock transactions, social posts, and news articles from a specific sector over a two-year period. This study employs cutting-edge natural language processing and machine learning techniques to uncover the connections between social and financial activity. Notably, we've identified that posts from corporate management are more closely linked to share price movements than those from retail investors, with posts receiving more public engagement also having a greater impact on share price fluctuations.

In the context of three-dimensional uniform sensor networks, we explore the challenge of placing wireless sensors within a three-dimensional bounded area. We're given a limited number of sensors (n) and a maximum allowable sensor separation distance (r), which defines the minimum distance between each sensor to maintain a network with uniform spacing. We're tasked with finding the optimal sensor arrangement that maximizes the total number of sensors in a 3D grid, subject to a given number of sensors (n), a specified sensor separation distance (r), and a bounded communication area in the shape of a prolate spheroid. We're particularly interested in this problem in the context of 3D sensor networks used in power systems for monitoring and control purposes. To this end, we introduce a novel algorithm that places sensors in a sequence of concentric 3D cubes, which allows for an efficient and optimal placement of sensors in a uniform 3D network subject to a given sensor separation distance.

A novel eigenstate selection method has been developed, combining quantum measurements and classical post-processing to achieve optimal performance. This algorithm can identify the correct eigenstate with a probability proportional to the target eigenstate's quality, at a computational cost proportional to the target eigenstate's degree. This stands in contrast to existing methods, which can accurately determine the target eigenstate's existence but necessitate multiple quantum measurements and classical processing commensurate with the complexity of the target eigenstate's annihilator polynomial. This research showcases the application of this algorithm in resolving quantum linear problems, where the use of multiple eigenstates enables solutions with a probability proportional to the product of the target eigenstate's quality and its counterpart. Notably, this method offers a higher probability than traditional methods such as amplitude amplification at a lower computational cost, when the target eigenstate's quality is high, and the target eigenstate's degree is lower than its annihilator complexity.

We initially examine the groundbreaking discovery of compact infant skyrmions made possible by combining electric and magnetic fields in a non-linear material. To achieve this, we consider the material to be a non-linear version of a well-studied compound that exhibits topological properties when doped with electric charges. By applying a gauge field in this context, we discover that the static low-energy dynamics of the infant skyrmions can be accurately described using an adapted version of the 't'Hooft-Polyakov action. In this study, we extend the understanding of these infant skyrmions by generalizing the action further to incorporate compact compactified and non-linear electric and magnetic gauge fields. By doing so, we uncover a previously unexplored complex structure within the infant skyrmions that can be visualized as a three-dimensional representation of a well-studied mathematical concept known as a Hopf bundle, where the compactified skyrmions are shown to reside within a complex three-dimensional space.

This research examines the potential for discovering unconventional interactions, particularly in the context of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). SMEFT represents a well-established framework for analyzing new physics phenomena, offering a reliable method to investigate various phenomena, such as those not predicted by the Standard Model, and those that it predicts but has yet to be observed. SMEFT effectively addresses the issue of flavour change, providing an essential framework for studying the properties of heavy flavours. Furthermore, the study of electroweak processes enables the exploration of additional Higgs couplings, allowing for a deeper understanding of the nature of the Higgs boson. By analyzing the results from the current Tevatron, LHC, and future high-energy colliders, the potential for discovering SMEFT interactions, particularly in the four-fermion operators, is assessed.

A state-of-the-art laboratory containing a rotating diamond feature has been developed, where a gyroscope built from a suspended diamond crystal within a MEMS device has demonstrated exceptional performance and stability. The setup boasts minimal mechanical and electrical interference and maintains thermal stability through active control and a passive shielding mechanism. Initially, the system achieved an impressive record of 4.4 degrees of freedom isolation from room temperature fluctuations. Furthermore, it successfully maintained a record of 1.2 degrees of freedom isolation for nearly 24 hours. The setup's design and functionality are thoroughly explained and highlighted through various tests that showcase its potential. Future plans for this project involve incorporating additional components such as atomic clocks and magnetometers to support quantum sensing applications.

This work outlines the present understanding of complete-cell simulation techniques, emphasizing the development of a framework that enables researchers to integrate and expand existing models. We suggest key areas for focus in advancing the field and propose experimental methods for confirming the accuracy of simulations through the creation of a reference data set.

This paper introduces a mobile multi-view object visual search system capable of identifying an object of interest across various devices and multiple perspectives. The technique not only determines if a matching object exists but also provides a ranked listing of object matches. To improve the search process, multiple views from both query and matching databases are utilized. However, due to limited network bandwidth, object features cannot be directly transferred from devices to a central server. To overcome this challenge, a novel search algorithm is developed that employs a unique binary code representation, enabling efficient matching score computation on each device and subsequent aggregation of scores from multiple views on the server. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through extensive testing on a large dataset, showing it outperforms traditional methods under practical conditions of limited data views.

A novel computing framework known as Hyperdimensional (HD) computing, which draws inspiration from the principles of human cognition. The HD framework has shown potential in developing efficient and robust classifiers for signal processing applications. In this research, we investigate the effectiveness of two strategic approaches, namely, feature selection and ensemble learning, in enhancing the performance of HD classifiers for the classification of seizures in long-term EEG recordings. The findings demonstrate that by integrating these strategies with the original HD approach, a state-of-the-art performance can be achieved for a specific EEG dataset. Notably, the proposed HD model exhibits compactness, allowing it to be deployed on low-power devices such as wearable technology for real-time monitoring.

Future observations of dark matter particles are highly likely to be made by researchers.  A possible method to investigate these particles involves the use of gravitational waves from binary black holes, which can serve as a new means of gaining insight into the universe's expansion history.  A recent discovery of the LIGO-Virgo Collaboration of a binary black hole, OJAs, has sparked interest in using such events as a 'dark Siren.'  A future Deci-hertz gravitational wave observatory is expected to detect a large number of binary black holes, which can provide a more accurate estimate of the Hubble constant.  A simulation was conducted to determine the maximum number of binary black holes detectable by a future Deci-hertz observatory, and the results were used to gain a more precise understanding of the Hubble constant.  A binary black hole pair detected by LISA will enable a more accurate estimate of the Hubble constant with a 10% margin of error.  Additionally, a binary black hole pair detected by LISA will allow scientists to gain insight into the universe's expansion history, and the method can be used to determine the Hubble constant with a 13% margin of error.

We have developed a multilingual corpus called QALD-9-plus, containing 1,371 questions across 10 languages, enabling queries on both DBpedia and Wikidata. Human interpreters from diverse linguistic backgrounds provide detailed responses to each question, providing a rich resource for both query understanding and database interpretation. As the first publicly accessible multilingual benchmark, QALD-9-plus, offers a challenging task for natural language processing models in the context of inquiry responding, thereby facilitating comparative evaluations across languages.

In recent years, researchers have developed various methods to analyze and summarize machine learning model outcomes, but most studies have focused on specific application domains. Instead, this study explores the cross-pollination of ideas between fields to find commonalities and differences in analyzing model outcomes, examining how techniques from natural language processing can be applied to computer vision tasks and vice versa. A new approach, using a measure called "Hindsight Summarization", is proposed to quantify the value of insights derived from different methods, providing a framework to evaluate them quantitatively and qualitatively. Ultimately, this study aims to establish a standard for comparing insights across different fields, suggesting a new approach for aggregating and weighing them to inform more effective decision-making.

Detecting bias in image datasets is crucial due to its adverse effects on model performance and fairness. Our focus is on detecting inherent bias across various domains, particularly in medical settings where underdiagnosis and misdiagnosis can be severe. We introduce a framework that utilizes two distinct approaches: the first employs diffusion maps to highlight domain-specific differences, and the second applies vector differences between sample pairs to pinpoint specific differences. By combining these methods, we identify clusters within a dataset, and a fairness metric is developed to quantify cluster imbalances. Our proposed solutions are tested using actual datasets, including the Skin Cancer and Breast Cancer Histology datasets, and show promising results in detecting intrinsic bias.

The success of many computer vision tasks heavily relies on the metric learning approach. However, the metric learning method is not very robust to noisy labels, especially when the training dataset contains many incorrect labels. Existing methods for handling noisy labels in metric learning have mainly focused on label filtering or incorporating a clean subset to guide the training process, without fully considering the noise caused by inaccurate comparisons between image pairs. This type of noise can significantly affect model generalization. To overcome this limitation, the current research proposes a new method called Proxy-Anchored Metric Learning (PAML). PAML aims to improve the robustness of metric learning to noisy labels by leveraging the relationships between proxies (representations of images) and anchors (image pairs). To this end, the method introduces a new loss function called the Sleek loss, which is designed to minimize the differences between the distances between proxies and anchors. The method leverages the relationships between proxies and anchors to estimate the noise level in the dataset. Experimental results show that PAML outperforms other methods in metric learning under noisy conditions.

We examine the validity of large-scale structure predictions made by modern cosmological simulations. By extending the quasilinear density gradient adjustment method, we've developed a new correlation function that is free of artificial force effects. Our analysis shows it produces a significantly different shape compared to conventional quasilinear correlation functions. However, when testing this function against data from various simulations, we found it fails to accurately predict power on cosmological scales above 100 Mpc, resulting in an estimated maximum precision of 0.035 in power spectrum measurements and 0.025 in correlation function power levels. Our findings suggest that a more thorough approach beyond the quasilinear region is necessary to achieve reliable cosmological constraints from simulations. We've also shown that power spectrum measurements on small scales can be overly sensitive to inaccurate predictions on larger scales, potentially causing inaccuracies in parameter estimation.

A theoretical framework for understanding topological SO(5) superconductivity has been proposed.
The study reveals that SO(5) superconductivity can be broken down into multiple components.
The research focuses on the SO(2) and SO(3) components, which are found to exhibit topological behavior in specific lattices.
A SO(4) time-reversal invariant topological superconducting phase is also discovered in certain lattices.
The research further explores the emergence of Majorana flat-bands in specific conditions.
The study's findings provide a clear theoretical basis for experimental studies of SO(5) superconductivity.
The research's results are expected to facilitate further experimental studies.
The study's theoretical framework is also found to be applicable to other systems of p-wave superconductors.

Silicon Micro Pattern Detectors (MAPDs) offer superior performance characteristics 
including low noise levels, high photoelectric sensitivity and fast response times. 
When exposed to a gas mixture featuring a high electron scattering frequency, MAPD 
detectors demonstrate an advantage over silicon diodes and diode-based arrays. 
Recent research has showcased the effectiveness of MAPD detectors in avalanche 
amplification, with a specific focus on utilizing MAPD arrays in high-energy 
astrophysics, particularly in the detection of gamma rays and charged particles. 
This study presents MAPD array avalanche detectors optimized for use in the 
detection of low-energy ions within a gas-filled environment, with a specific 
application in cosmic ray muon detection.

In noncommutative algebraic geometry, the cyclic homoclinic cover offers a crucial tool for analyzing singularities, and its properties reveal intricate relationships. Research has demonstrated that the homoclinic cover's exponents are interconnected with those of the original ring. Building upon this understanding, a more general framework has been developed by defining higher-order "partial homoclinic covers" for noncommutative rings. These constructs reveal a connection to a generalization of Serre's conjecture and exhibit symmetry between left and right ring projections. Furthermore, this extension shows that the partial homoclinic cover's exponents are maximized when the original ring is a Cohen-Macaulay ring.

A nuclear method called differential diffusion analysis, which utilizes collected data from multiple
experiments, is used to study the temperature-induced changes in the magnetic properties of Aurivillius oxide
materials, specifically those with composition Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$. This material's behavior is studied under high pressure
over a temperature range from 50 to 300 K. Our findings show that Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ is in a ferrimagnetic
state at low temperatures. Increasing the temperature leads to a shift towards a state of partial magnetic ordering,
where the material is no longer fully magnetized, due to a change in the material's magnetic structure. The material is
found to remain partially magnetized at room temperature when it is at high pressures of up to 2 GPa. This material is
showing a new type of behavior under high pressures of 2 to 3.5 GPa, where the material is in a phase transition
state, accompanied by a change in the material's magnetic properties, by the temperature, and by the pressure. This
research suggests that the material is in a phase transition state, where the material is in a phase change process, by
the application of a certain pressure, by the application of a certain temperature, and by the partial magnetization.

A broker's charges are a crucial aspect to many investors, with some levying fees per trade and others, like Robinhood, charge a flat fee, while still imposing small fees per share. This research presents a Bayesian analysis that allows investors to compare the costs of different brokers based on their pricing structures and the volume of their trading. The study provides a ranking of several prominent brokers, including Fidelity, Robinhood, and Vanguard, to estimate the trading expenses incurred by each, finding that Robinhood is generally the most cost-effective for large orders but that a more detailed analysis reveals this may not always be the case. This research also highlights a potential disadvantage of Robinhood's business model, where it may dig into its profits to gain market share.

Optomechanical add-drop filters are a crucial component in optical communication systems, enabling efficient signal routing by combining optical and mechanical movement. However, their practical implementation is restricted by low frequency and limited tunability. In this research, we propose a new type of optomechanical add-drop filter that operates across a wide range of frequencies, effectively making it a frequency-independent device. By utilizing a specially designed waveguide with an adjustable refractive index, we have developed a system where the optical mode can be manipulated by a movable boundary while maintaining minimal mechanical impact. As a result, we have discovered that this device can be easily tuned over a wide range of frequencies, from 10^14 to 10^16 Hz, using a relatively small mechanical displacement.

The Internet has become an essential resource for collecting data and informing research, and its influence extends to social services and community health. This dual use raises concerns about data credibility, particularly in web-based materials such as social media, forums, and blogs. We conducted an analysis of this digital output, categorized as 'gray' data. We evaluated the content of three social media platforms, Twitter, Reddit, and a community blog, to understand their utility in research. We found that Twitter posts are generally short-term events-focused, suitable for real-time analysis of community interest and event prediction. In contrast, Reddit's community engagement forums provide a more in-depth view of topics and participants. We observed that forums are often associated with real-world events and specific social groups. We found that a community blog serves as an information resource and a platform for discussion, which can be analyzed to reveal local details, community growth, and user participation patterns. Our study highlights the benefits and limitations of using these online platforms for research. We found that by combining data from various sources, we can gain a more comprehensive understanding of community dynamics.

The vast amount of image data generated globally necessitates efficient compression of large datasets without loss to maintain their usability. Although lossy image compression offers superior speed, end-to-end trained neural networks deliver state-of-the-art performance, whereas lossless image compression is preferred by preserving image integrity and original metadata. PILC, a comprehensive framework, utilizes advanced techniques like predictive image coding and multi-scale feature learning from deep neural networks to create an image lossless and predictive coding network with end-to-end training capabilities. We introduce a neural image quality assessment model, PILC-Assess, to evaluate the overall quality of the compressed images. Experimental results demonstrate PILC surpasses state-of-the-art lossless image compression methods, including those from the CALIC, B44, and CALIC-B44, with a significant improvement of 34.60%, 16.41%, and 16.39% on the PSNR metric respectively, accompanied by a 1.84x, 1.29x, and 1.27x speedup. Furthermore, our PILC-Assess model exhibits a 1.84x, 1.29x, and 1.27x performance boost over the original versions of the same metrics.

For the first time, the B+ to Ds+ KF decay has been observed using data from proton-proton collisions gathered by the LHCb detector at 8 and 13 TeV center-of-mass energies, corresponding to 2 and 1.0 fb^-1 of integrated luminosity. This analysis found the B+ to Ds+ KF branching fraction to be (11.8±0.4±0.3±0.3±0.2) × 10^-6, with the first uncertainty source being the statistical sample, the second related to the calibration of the absolute branching fraction scale, the third due to systematic uncertainties and the fourth due to the uncertainty in the B^0 to Ds- K+K- branching fraction. Furthermore, the B+ to Ds+ KF branching fraction is significantly more than the predicted by the Standard Model, the B+ to Ds+ phi decay.

The sensitivity of optimal transport problems to the underlying metrics has been a long-standing concern. Recent work has addressed this by modifying the definition of optimal transport to prioritize distance resilience. Our approach takes a distinct path, examining how robust solutions can be identified efficiently, and demonstrating that this framework has equivalent effectiveness as our original definition in certain circumstances. This research was motivated by the practical need to counter the impact of data corruption and anomalies on statistical learning tasks.

In this research, we explore a novel method of training artificial intelligence teammates that collaborate with humans in various tasks by modeling their cooperation through a Markov decision process. The model enables us to derive optimal strategies for cooperative play, and also allows for the development of intelligent teammates that can work alongside humans in a coordinated manner. By combining this approach with reinforcement learning, we are able to train AI teammates that can effectively partner with humans in a range of activities, including the selection of shared goals and communication processes. Through simulations, we demonstrate that the learned strategies result in AI teammates that can choose between competing goals based on their priority, communicate effectively, and provide valuable suggestions, ultimately leading to superior overall performance compared to other models.

The supersymmetry theory's potential is safeguarded against ultra-violet corrections by its fundamental principle, demonstrating invariance under a new symmetry called manifest auxiliary supersymmetry.  A comprehensive framework for modeling and simulating complex quantum systems, based on graph theory, classifies a unique type of graph invariant called an edge-forest, which ensures that a theory remains ultraviolet safe while preserving supersymmetry.  Applying graph invariance, a new class of actions is defined that protect robust supersymmetry against corrections up to the four-dimensional four-loop level.  Furthermore, a representation theory for the graph invariance is established and used to construct a robust supersymmetric non-supersymmetric SU(N) gauge theory, in which the gauge group is a product of independent U(1) groups, each with a different number of fermions.  The theory is shown to be ultraviolet safe while preserving supersymmetry and remaining non-supersymmetric, and potentially offers a new class of general models for strong and weak unification based on a product gauge group.

Disciplines like engineering, biology, and economics rely heavily on visualization skills to enhance understanding and communication of visualization results. Various professions require similar visualization skills, but often require different types of expertise. This study investigates how experts in one field perform in tasks requiring high visual and spatial skills by comparing them against non-experts. Results show that individuals with expertise in one field can develop similar visual and spatial skills as experts in that field, but may not reach the same level as experts from another field. Interestingly, the type of expertise required does not seem to impact one's ability to perform spatial tasks. Furthermore, the study reveals that individuals with expertise in one field may still benefit from training on visual and spatial skills, as it can improve their performance. Ultimately, the findings suggest that visual and spatial skills may be developed through practice and training, rather than being an innate characteristic of a particular field or discipline.

We present a novel loop construct, referred to as Clause Set Loors, which enables the definition of loops with a high level of abstraction by specifying a loop body related to a divisor of the loop's iteration count. To analyze the termination of such loops, we have developed a termination function that utilizes inductive reasoning. This function, when applied to a program, determines whether it can be proven terminable through the application of inductive reasoning. Our termination function has been implemented as a plugin for the Coq proof system, allowing users to easily define loops with a divisor as the iteration count and establish termination through the specified method.

In recent years, graph-based data models have gained prominence, and researchers have proposed various ways to project and extract graph representations from non-graph domains. However, existing methods often require substantial modifications to either the data or the model, and lack a unified approach to consider multiple data models and structures. To address this, we introduce a novel framework that aligns two flexible graph models by optimizing node embeddings, allowing for seamless graph extraction. By developing and applying our framework to real-world data, we demonstrate that this method produces high-quality graph representations and outperforms existing approaches in several key features.

Deep learning models are commonly used in Analytical Mechanical Modeling to model the steady-state behavior of complex systems, such as neural ODEs for parameterized mechanical systems. However, these models often struggle with generalization to unseen data, particularly when there are significant differences between the training and evaluation distributions. To address this limitation, this study introduces a novel loss function that incorporates the transient dynamics of mechanical systems, enabling better performance on out-of-distribution data. The new loss function, inspired by NLP advancements, improves the transfer learning performance of neural ODEs on a variety of tasks, such as system identification and control, even when training data significantly differs from evaluation data.

A new framework is developed to address contentious issues in power distribution by developing fair algorithms for cost sharing mechanisms. The approach is applied to both linear and nonlinear power functions with the goal of achieving efficient divisions that satisfy certain pre-determined criteria. These algorithms are specifically designed to ensure that each site's share does not exceed a specified percentage of its own power, and the overall total share meets another constraint. The framework's efficacy is demonstrated through numerical experiments that validate its effectiveness in providing equitable power allocations.

Credible news outlets typically maintain objectivity regarding political controversies, but differentiate themselves through occurrence coreference resolution, an essential aspect of reporting on such events. This study addresses occurrence coreference resolution by proposing two methods: one utilizing a robust transfer model linked to an existing dataset of identical events and another employing a pre-trained multilingual transformer model fine-tuned on in-house data. To assess the performance of these approaches, a newly developed dataset of 1,500 news articles covering 500 controversies was created, with an additional 1,800 paragraphs from multiple sources on the web collected for benchmarking purposes. The results of a thorough evaluation reveal that a pre-trained transformer model fine-tuned on in-house data outperforms the alternative methods, with an average F1 score of 0.958 on the created dataset and 0.876 on the benchmark dataset.

The Complementarity Knapsack Problem, a mixed-integer nonlinear program with complementarity constraints, is a challenging nonlinear program. Solving it numerically is complicated by complementarity conditions that can be difficult to satisfy. A proposed model reformulation using a Knapsack Complementarity Problem formulation may provide a more straightforward solution process. This paper introduces a novel category of optimality criteria based on the Complementarity Knapsack Problem, derived from the first-order necessary conditions of Karush-Kuhnau for non-linear optimization problems with complementarity constraints. It then demonstrates how these conditions relate to the first-order conditions of the Complementarity Knapsack Problem. Furthermore, the paper outlines a method to utilize the novel optimality criteria to develop a new category of NLP-based facially-expressed constraints, referred to as Facet Complementarity Knapsack Issues. These Facet Complementarity Knapsack Issues are then used to reformulate the original nonlinear program into a polyhedral form that can be solved more efficiently through cutting plane methods.

This paper defines and explores $I$-admissible derivations for semiprime algebras with a fixed ideal $I$. Key properties and relationships of these derivations are established, along with associated concepts including $I$-admissible Jordan derivations and centralizers. The concepts are further utilized in characterizing finite dimensional semisimple algebras under the condition of having only trivial $I$-admissible derivations.

We reconcile Weinberg's method with helicity constraints to derive a formula for the two-parameter strong CP violation in a chiral theory, demonstrating it yields the same result as his method. The separate approaches offer unique insights into the underlying mechanisms.

We are examining the transversal of a nonlinear mapping X, which is distinct from a linear mapping context. A nonlinear transversal is comprised of a family of curves X and corresponding vectors at each point. This concept is analogous to a linear map's transversal but is defined using function spaces and measures. This work extends the transversal concept and introduces the nonlinear Favard length, a measure of a function's irregularity off a given interval. The Favard length has applications in nonlinear mapping contexts and is connected to moduli of smoothness. The study also explores connections between the transversal and moduli problems for nonlinear mappings. The investigation includes a special case of a nonlinear transversal created by iterating a linear mapping with a scalar function, which is related to the Favard length and has a probabilistic interpretation. The work introduces a modified transversal concept, which is a subset of the original but is defined using a different measure. The two transversal groups are related to the convergence of sums of iterates of the mapping. The study also examines the convergence conditions for the sum of iterates of a nonlinear mapping.

We introduce a novel algorithm called Direct Policy Search via Dynamic Tube (Direct-PT), a more efficient alternative to traditional black box optimization methods. By utilizing a sophisticated tube model that adapts to system dynamics, Direct-PT significantly improves the sample complexity and speed, outperforming existing techniques. The algorithm's effectiveness is further enhanced through the incorporation of a novel mimicry objective, enabling the generation of stable trajectories with reduced interaction costs. The proposed method demonstrates substantial improvements over state-of-the-art approaches in challenging simulation environments.

The anomalous Hall effect, resulting from a breakdown in inversion symmetry, has far more significance in the field of spintronics than initially thought.  While the second-order Hall voltage due to the Berry curvature is well understood, research on the anomalous Hall effect of the third order is still in its infancy.  To address this gap, a comprehensive study based on a modified semiclassical theory has been conducted, examining how third-order Hall voltages arise from not only Berry curvature but also from other third-order curvature not considered in conventional applications.  As a result, a new form of spin Hall current has been discovered, featuring a spin orientation in the direction of current rather than perpendicular to it.  This discovery paves the way for developing a new class of third-order Hall devices.

The task of creating compact representations for sets of call graphs, like set covers and sketches, has garnered significant attention in recent years. Researchers have been working to develop methods for analyzing large datasets of call graphs, like those found in Fortune's collection, using advanced techniques to compare the structural properties of these call graphs. Building on the success of previous studies in generating universal sets of call graphs, this research aims to develop a method for creating efficient representations of large collections of call graphs, with a focus on their ability to compare groups of call graphs and identify their unique characteristics. To measure the quality of these representations, this paper proposes a metric that captures how well the representation aligns with the original call graphs, allowing for both lower bounds on the optimal representation and the evaluation of developed algorithms. Using this metric, this research presents a new universal set of call graphs that is more efficient in terms of storage and comparison time, with a comprehensive analysis of its performance relative to existing solutions.

A widely used text corpus called the One Billion Words corpus has become the benchmark for evaluating the effectiveness of language models. This study examines the advantages and disadvantages of the original corpus. While it is considered representative of the overall structure of language, it is primarily composed of articles, which significantly limits its versatility in testing and understanding language diversity. Furthermore, the study highlights potential pitfalls in the methods used to create and analyze the corpus. As the standard for evaluating the performance and development of language models, it is essential to reassess and improve the standards used to create and evaluate these models to make them more reliable and comprehensive.

High-resolution X-ray and soft gamma-ray wave oscillations at flare sites are linked to the plasma processes in the flare current sheet. The plasma oscillations are influenced by the mirror mode, Kelvin-Helmholtz, and other instabilities, causing the oscillations to exhibit complex behaviors. The plasma density in the current sheet is a key factor that affects the oscillations. The plasma density is affected by the outflows from the flare site, causing the oscillations to display unique patterns. Through numerical simulations, we found that the plasma density in the current sheet decreases as the plasma flows out. The decrease in density leads to the mirror mode instability growing more rapidly. As a result, flare oscillations often exhibit quasi-periodic patterns. By tracking the plasma density and magnetic field at the flare site, we can infer the current sheet's properties, such as thickness and plasma density. The findings suggest that observing the oscillations at the flare site can provide valuable information about the current sheet's structure.

This study introduces a novel anomaly detection method rooted in the concept of the Fourier Transform, incorporating the Contrary function to enhance image clarity and preserve edge details. Contrary, a multi-scale feature extractor, utilizes convolutional operations in various layers to generate a ranking of image content. Based on this ranking, the input image is reconstructed and refined through the Contrary function. Subsequently, the refined image serves as the basis for a Fourier Transform analysis, generating a feature vector used to evaluate anomalies in industrial images. Performance was assessed through comparative experiments with established methods on the MVTec dataset, with additional real-world experiments demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed approach.

The study focuses on a modified KP-I equation incorporating a small parameter, $
u$, related to the dispersion function, $e^{2ih|x]|h|^{-2b}$. The analysis is centered around constructing solutions with minimal irregularity by leveraging the $
u$ parameter. A broader class of initial data $u_0$ in $H^s\cap L^{ rac{1}{2}}_{|h|<1}$ is considered for some $s>3/2$, along with an additional $L^{ rac{1}{2}}_{|h<1}$ assumption. It is shown that low regularity solutions with minimal irregularity $\lesssim 
u^{-(s-3/2)}$ can be obtained for solutions within the space $L^2\left(\mathbb R, (1+|h|^{2b-1})^{-1+4/2
u}ight)$.

The time-reversal symmetry plays a vital role in understanding the properties of quantum systems. Kramers' theorem establishes that degenerate states in time-reversible Hamiltonians are double-degenerate. This symmetry is broken when these systems interact with external noise, leading to the breakdown of Kramers' degeneracy. Conversely, this degeneracy can also be restored in noisy environments under specific conditions. Our research investigates the underlying causes of this restoration by analyzing the behavior of noisy Kramers' degenerate systems within scenarios of local interactions and dissipation. Our findings indicate that this restoration results from the formation of degeneracy in energy subspaces, rather than the individual energy levels themselves. This breakdown-synthesis-reestablishment of Kramers' degeneracy is influenced by the spin dimension and the ratio of system-environment interaction strengths. Our research offers new insights into the behavior of Kramers' degenerate systems under dissipation and provides practical guidance for designing solutions to maintain and restore this symmetry in quantum devices.

In highly-mobile 5G networks and beyond, predicting future responses from CSI in time is crucial, enabling the design of more efficient communication networks. A new deep learning model has been proposed that can accurately forecast three or more consecutive CSI responses at the receiver end without the need for additional transmission overhead, leveraging the correlation in preceding CSI responses and the channel characteristics shared by both transmitter and receiver. This model outperforms traditional baseline methods and remains unaffected by changes in channel conditions, demonstrating its scalability for use in mobile networks and low-complexity hardware. A thorough analysis of its training parameters revealed the optimal conditions for optimal performance.

We present a novel approach for determining the size of a region of interest within an image, represented by a disparity measure, based on a mixture of beta density functions. By utilizing maximum likelihood estimation, we obtain the parameters of the mixture model. An efficient method for estimating the parameters, a two-step EM algorithm, is introduced and compared to the standard multi-step EM algorithm. Both methods are applied to both real and synthetic data, utilizing the SIFT and HOG disparity measures. The results indicate that the two-step EM algorithm yields the best performance with the HOG disparity measure.

We establish the convergence of the Szegő kernel on Grauert cylinders as the transformation group's order tends towards infinity. Consequently, this outcome leads to the derivation of a Szegő exponent for these specific manifolds, which are defined as the total curvature of their Weil-Petersson metric.

Renaming rows and columns in a matrix to rectify an existing Line Chart can be a complex task. This paper presents two distinct approaches to solving this problem, referred to as MARINLINGA and Rous, named after their respective inventors. MARINLINGA involves utilizing a set of rules to relabel rows and columns, ensuring a specific set of criteria is met. Rous, on the other hand, employs iterative labeling techniques to rename rows and columns in an effort to optimize data representation. Although both methods share the goal of producing charts that meet specific criteria, they differ significantly in their method of operation. To illustrate this difference, a comprehensive example is provided, highlighting the situations in which each method excels.

This article proves a claim by Lee-Lee, which suggests that a commutative ring R having at least three elements and having properties such that its local rings R_p in any prime decomposition and their unique prime subfields p_1,...,p_k are related in a certain way. Specifically, it is related in that the free module on (p_1,...,p_k) contains a submodule which is isomorphic to the direct sum of the modules R_p over p_1,...,p_k. This proof has additional applications, such as a result stating that a commutative ring R having properties such as being to pull back algebras and having a unique prime factorization will have a module which is isomorphic to the direct sum of the modules R_p over p_1,...,p_k. Additionally, it is shown that a commutative ring R having properties such as being to pull back algebras and having a unique prime factorization will have a module which is isomorphic to the direct sum of the modules R_p over p_1,...,p_k.

To keep up with rapidly evolving software systems, developers often apply flexible coding standards, like adopting third-party libraries, to mitigate the complexity of maintaining large-scale projects. This study investigates the reliability of these standards by analyzing the extent of dependency redundancy in a significant number of Java open-source software packages. By analyzing the behavior of 12 prominent libraries and how their inclusion affects 6 popular frameworks, our research found most libraries's features are only used once, yet nearly one-third of code changes introduce new dependencies on existing libraries. These findings suggest that developers should carefully weigh the benefits and drawbacks of incorporating redundant dependencies when deciding how to incorporate third-party code into their projects.

The concept of entangled two-photon states has been applied in quantum walks on graphs to create quantum entanglement over spatial space. However, entanglement vanishes due to measurement-induced non-locality (MIS) when one particle is measured. To preserve biphoton entanglement, a new approach utilizing intertwined state vectors has been introduced. This approach aims to maintain biphoton entanglement during quantum computation tasks, such as searching for a marked vertex in a quantum walk. Two entangled two-photon states with opposite signs are combined in a syntheses protocol to achieve biphoton entanglement preservation. The sign of the coin operator plays a crucial role in maintaining biphoton entanglement, which is referred to as the "relation" property. Conversely, the absence of biphoton entanglement is referred to as the "hostility" property. Our findings indicate that not all biphoton entanglement can be maintained throughout the quantum computation process. Specifically, the "relation" property is lost after the first coin operator, whereas the "hostility" property is lost immediately at the beginning of the syntheses protocol.

We're tackling a range of multistage stochastic control and resiliency problems, incorporating diverse scenarios to minimize potential impacts from uncertain system changes. To balance the need for comprehensive consideration and computational feasibility, we're using a weighted average of multiple scenario sets, weighing their effectiveness based on performance against the range of considered scenarios. To optimize this, we're identifying more efficient scenario sets with comparable weighted performance, thereby reducing the overall number of considered scenarios. To achieve this, we're using a novel concept called total variation discrepancy for assessing the relative significance of scenarios. Our approach is demonstrated through applications in two problems, one optimizing inventory and reserve, and another ensuring electric supply chain liquidity during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Recently, researchers have been working to predict actions in a sequence by learning the dynamics of a task step by step. Most existing methods rely on a model that's trained to predict the next feature in a sequence, but this can be inaccurate because it's based on the assumption that it's easy to predict the next action in a sequence, when in reality it might be impossible to predict any action. To address this issue, we've developed a model that uses a complex feature mapping technique to recognize patterns in a sequence, which allows the model to recognize these patterns in a more general way. We've also developed a way to represent these patterns in a probabilistic way, which enables the model to predict when a pattern is likely to occur in a sequence. To train our model, we introduce a new learning method that adapts the dynamics of a sequence to match the patterns we've learned. We've tested our model on various action prediction tasks and found that it outperforms existing models.

A novel approach to the Einstein-de Haas effect combines the principles of thermodynamics and magnetism, resulting in a phenomenon where a rotating ferromagnet produces heat due to the conversion of angular momentum into magnetic moments. This phenomenon can be explained by a solution to the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, resulting in a unique change in temperature, achieved by solving a coupled system of partial differential equations. By employing a solvable framework based on deep thermalization, the proposed approach yields a more accurate representation of the heat produced, as evidenced by numerical results.

Consider a homogeneous tree of infinite depth and infinite breadth as the space X, and define the pseudo-differential operator ∗ by using the Sobolev function σ from L^2(X) functions to L^2(X) functions. We establish that the operator ∐ is bounded and Hilbert-Schmidt on L^2(X), but not trace class, and that the convolution operator ∙ is bounded and compact on C(X), where C(X) denotes the continuous functions on X. We also show that the operator ∙ is not bounded on C(X), and that the convolution operator ∐ is not compact on L^∞(X), with L^∞(X) as the space of bounded functions.

Our research demonstrates the capability of mobile devices to detect nearby cellular infrastructure, reveals the impact of such knowledge on 5G network performance, and identifies differences in detection methods used by major carriers. Our study shows that detecting nearby cell towers is feasible with widely available smartphone technologies, and our data indicates that 5G carriers employ unique detection methods, including the use of 4G/3G networks for detection purposes. Our findings also suggest that users who enable software features to query nearby cell towers experience improved 5G connection speeds by up to 19% in high-traffic scenarios.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) often overestimate their accuracy when encountering unknown samples. This overconfidence issue can be mitigated by incorporating an additional module, known as the Chamer Out-of-Distribution (CODE), into the DNN, allowing it to identify and discard uncertain inputs. The CODE module is comprised of two geometric shape-based submodules. Firstly, the Unfolded CODE (UCODE) folds complex shapes into simpler 1D patterns and utilizes a fully connected neural network to learn from these patterns. Secondly, the Folding CODE (FCODE) clusters input data by mapping it into a 1D pattern and utilizes a convolutional neural network to generate low-dimensional features. By employing either of these modules, the CODE model successfully identifies and filters out unknown samples, thereby preventing overconfidence.

Using data collected from high-energy proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV, analyzed with a subevent CMS algorithm, researchers have calculated the distribution of nearby azimuthal angles between two prominent jets. The results show that 2-jet, 3-jet, and 4-jet events exhibit characteristic patterns of away-side and near-side angular correlations, which differ in their shapes as the number of jets increases. The study also explores the dependence of these patterns on jet transverse momenta and of subevent algorithms on their parameters.

The increasing reliance on machine learning in image recognition and classification has been hindered by the scarcity of detailed annotations for a wide range of images, which has led to the development of semi-supervised and unsupervised deep learning techniques. This research paper provides a comprehensive review of the evolution of semi-supervised and unsupervised deep learning methods, encompassing image classification, active learning, and few-shot learning. By examining established semi-supervised and unsupervised deep learning techniques and recent advancements in deep learning, this study identifies the need to integrate deep learning with these semi-supervised and unsupervised methods and proposes a new framework for semi-supervised and unsupervised deep learning. This framework outlines potential research directions and provides new insights into the development of semi-supervised and unsupervised deep learning.

Identifying and correcting outliers is crucial in 3D reconstruction, yet existing approaches primarily focus on specific environments like structures and cities, leaving a significant knowledge gap. This paper presents RECol, a pioneering 3D reconstruction technique centered around frame quality, introducing a novel metric - Reconstruction Error Frames - to effectively pinpoint and rectify 3D outliers. Through comprehensive experiments on diverse datasets, including indoor and outdoor environments featuring both artificial and natural objects, along with a newly created dataset centered on outdoor natural features, our method demonstrates superior performance in accurately labeling frames, with precise results on a newly established evaluation metric. Additionally, our approach yields high-quality, error-free reconstructions, while showcasing the potential of our framework in broader applications.

This paper explores the dynamical systems described by non-linear equations, specifically those in non-integrable or chaotic states, and examines similarities between their behavior and that of the Yorke-Environment model. We investigate how energy is transferred within these systems through the fractional derivative of their cross-correlation functions. Additionally, we discuss and compare the long-term patterns observed in cross-correlation functions of non-linear systems with those seen in the Yorke-Environment model for both consistent and non-consistent systems.

The Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) is used to investigate the Standard Model's limitations and to derive bounds for certain neutrino parameters. Research has been conducted on the lowest-order neutrino corrections, which are a key focus of this study. Specifically, the investigation centers on the low-energy effective field description of these corrections, which are a key area of interest. Two new results have been discovered through a global fit of experimental data: a non-zero value for the dimension six parameter ${\tilde \chi}_{tau}\chi_{eQ}$ of 0.16 is found at a 1 standard deviation confidence level, and the parameter $g_{aZ\tau\tau}$ is also found non-zero at 0.17, one standard deviation.

The connection between a neuron and a glial cell's slow-moving ion channel creates a unique dynamic interaction that results in rhythmic activity when looked at from a multi-cell perspective, as seen in studies where various cell types are modeled together. This interaction is caused by how different cell types react to and affect each other through slow-moving cells and faster-moving cells. Neurons rely heavily on slow-moving cells for their activity, while glial cells use faster-moving channels. As a result of this interaction, the different cell types exhibit distinct reaction times with neurons reacting more quickly, and this interaction leads to the creation of rhythmic activity when looked at from a broad perspective of many cells.

We investigate a particle with spin-1/2, devoid of charge, situated within a background magnetic field, characterized by a complex vector potential denoted as $\mathbf{A}$. This study delves into the novel aspects of the non-Abelian geometric potential, specifically the Berry, Curl, and Magnetic Chern Numbers, as well as the Bohr-Sommerfeld integral, spin degeneracy, and quantum Stokes theorem. Furthermore, we examine the topological properties of the particle in the presence of this non-Abelian magnetic field, drawing a comparison with its Abelian counterpart under a given condition.

We are studying a one-dimensional, infinite cellular-automata model where a particle moves randomly, starting from the right-hand side of the grid and traveling one space to the left or right each time step, in a semi-infinite, one-dimensional lattice. The model is unique in that its space-time behavior is determined by the particle's movement, as opposed to fixed boundaries. When the particle hits a cell, it travels to the adjacent cell and leaves the initial cell empty. Initially, all cells are occupied by the particle. Our findings show that, over time, the particle tends to diffuse through the lattice, leaving behind a clean initial zone behind it. We have identified the speed at which this wavefront advances as the rate at which the particle moves, and have also calculated the amplitude of the wavefront in terms of the particle's movement speed and time step, for both circular and square shapes.

For a hyperbolic knot $K$, the natural map that assigns the formal semigroup $N_K$ to each representation $\rho: \Gamma\to SL_2(\mathbb{C})$ extends the Thurston decomposition of the mapping class group into hyperbolic transformations and pseudo-Anosov maps associated with $K$. This article investigates the properties of the image of the Thurston decomposition in $N_K$ for certain classes of hyperbolic knots, focusing on their structure as well as the behavior of pseudo-Anosov semigroups as the entropy increases.

A Poisson equation is derived for the Boltzmann collision operator on the space of radially dependent functions, using the Landau or Boltzmann model, which results in hydrodynamic equations. In the case of the Landau equation, the obtained equations differ from those obtained using the Boltzmann equation by incorporating a term representing the collisional relaxation of entropy. An explicit expression for the relaxation time is provided, which depends on the spatial dependence of the distribution function and the Coulomb logarithm.

In computer vision, object detection in live video streams, such as endoscopic procedures, is a widely researched area. Recent advancements in real-time high definition, coupled with the availability of open datasets, have led to the development of highly accurate models. This has significant implications for fields like medicine, where rapid object detection is crucial. This paper focuses on a unique application of object detection in real-time video feeds, namely the identification of endoscopic instruments during procedures. To improve model resilience, we employ ensemble learning techniques using BFGM and ADAM optimizers and a unique loss function that combines cross-entropy and mean average precision. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in real-world clinical settings, particularly in challenging instances where objects are partially occluded.

A widely observed phenomenon in source code filenames is the presence of syntax patterns comprised of letters and symbols not found in the basic alphabet, such as asterisks, underscores, and mixed-case letters. These syntax elements often appear at the start or end of filenames, and may be combined in various ways. Research indicates that understanding their syntax is essential for deciphering potential meanings, although the reverse isn't always true. In this research paper, we develop a systematic approach to categorize and define syntax patterns using a formal syntax specification. We also introduce the concept of semantic syntax, which considers the intended meaning behind a syntax pattern in source code. Empirical studies using over 200 million filenames from popular code repositories and 40,000 open-source projects demonstrate the effectiveness of our methodology in accurately identifying syntax patterns and accurately interpreting their meanings in source code contexts.

We create a new infinite-dimensional $\square_q$-structure derived from the affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, using the $q$-Dixmier-Malliavin algebra. This development is also connected to previous findings by Gelfand and MacEwan, as well as to a special case study by Lescot regarding the deformation of the Weyl algebra. We further investigate the underlying operator topology of the new structure.

The grain-growth kinetics in multi-phase systems can be understood through a model that accounts for the interactions between grains in separate phases. This model, known as the LSW theory, can be applied to three-phase systems by considering the influence of one phase on the growth of grains in the other two phases. Based on this, a computational model has been developed to simulate the evolution of grain structures in three-phase systems and study the effects of grain size distribution, mobility, and boundary energy on grain growth. The results show that when one phase is much thicker than the others, its growth is often limited by slow diffusion, while coarsening in the other two phases is typically limited by grain growth. However, in all scenarios, grain growth rate is significantly influenced by grain boundary energy. The developed computational model provides a tool for predicting grain structure and grain size distribution in complex multi-phase systems and can be applied to understand grain growth in various technological contexts.

Human pose estimation is a fundamental component of various computer vision and robotics research, with 3D human pose estimation being a crucial aspect. This work presents a comprehensive evaluation of cutting-edge models for 3D human pose estimation, with a focus on analyzing the techniques used by each. We provide a detailed comparison of the methods employed by each model, with a standard approach consisting of four key stages: image feature extraction, pose decoding, loss calculation, and optimization. This analysis is paired with a standard test framework for 3D human pose estimation, with 10 techniques and 9 benchmark methods used for evaluation. Our results indicate that the most effective methods for 3D human pose estimation are DeepPrior+ and DeepRoot+ when utilizing a stacked hourglass network, as well as Multi-Pose+ when utilizing a single column network. Interestingly, these models do not adhere to industry standards, with DeepPrior+ and Multi-Pose+ relying on a straightforward loss function, whereas DeepRoot+ employs a unique, more complex approach.

In our research, we demonstrate that superconductivity can occur in sites that are sparsely connected due to extremely strong electron-electron repulsion. Repulsive interactions are known to suppress superconductivity, but strong repulsion is observed in high-temperature superconductors and certain transition metal dichalcogenides. Our findings are applicable to systems with discrete or continuous symmetry, and we confirm that superconducting states are stable. We also discover that the critical interaction threshold for superconductivity is lower in systems with lower dimensionality. Our work provides a mathematical explanation for a previously observed phenomenon in experimental high-temperature superconductors.

To explain the observed electroweak symmetry breaking, a scalar leptoquark with a global U(1) symmetry baryon number is introduced. This model addresses neutrino oscillations and dark matter coannihilation issues simultaneously. Lepton flavor violation effects, such as $l_i \to l_j \gamma$ and $l_i l_j \to \gamma \gamma$, are constrained by experimental data, leading to a prediction of mass for the scalar leptoquark. If the leptoquark's mass is near 100 GeV, it can facilitate TeV-scale dark matter and a Higgs coupling to muons that aligns with the observed data.

The concept of category is a fundamental framework for comprehending the universe, allowing for the analysis of a wide range of subjects including psychology, human senses, operational systems, computational systems, and more. Notably, category theory has played a pivotal role in shaping the development of computer science and functional programming. Although artificial intelligence has existed for nearly four decades, category theory has only begun to significantly impact machine learning and other subfields of artificial intelligence over the past 15 years. This article provides a concise overview of category theory's application in machine learning and offers an assessment of its influence on this rapidly expanding field.

This paper presents a novel method for designing a high-order sliding mode controller with optimal endpoint recovery time for a class of second-order systems. The design process involves a two-stage procedure, with the first stage involving the application of the standard Lyapunov rule to determine the scalar factor of the sliding mode surface. Stage two involves integrating a dynamic surface controller to minimize endpoint recovery time. The paper further expands on the design process for second-order systems with multi-dimensional inputs and presents case studies to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

This research introduces a method that utilizes vibrational stress to gather
quantitative data on the layered configuration of active materials within lithium-ion
batteries at rest. By applying ultrasonic vibrations to a charged battery and
monitoring changes in its electrochemical response, this technique enables the
detection of two key changes - the initiation of diffusion and interface movement
between layers. The study derives mathematical expressions connecting the measured
responses to active material layer thickness. The calculated thickness values can be
used to evaluate how aging affects battery layers and influence battery performance.
The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through experiments on lithium-nickel-cobalt-manganese (NMC) 622 and all-solid-state battery cells.

This research introduces a novel discrete-time controller for a crane model, which utilizes a levelness-based control approach inspired by the concept of virtual frames. This innovative method is built upon a natural interpretation of levelness, which is transformed into a control strategy that targets the desired equilibrium state. In contrast to traditional feedback control methods, this levelness-based approach achieves stability without relying on specific system knowledge or feedback mechanisms. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that this levelness-based control outperforms traditional PID and LQR methods, showcasing its robustness and efficacy.

Weakly-supervised learning models for image-description rely heavily on a large dataset of paired images and captions, yet obtaining such a dataset can be difficult and expensive to compile. As a result, it is common to encounter substantial amounts of noisy captions within these datasets, significantly impairing model performance. This study presents an innovative approach called Collaborative Distillation, which enables the creation of robust, image-description models even when utilizing flawed training data. This method involves the simultaneous training of two models: a teacher, which is trained using a standard loss function, and a student, which is trained through collaborative learning with the teacher, utilizing a novel, adaptive loss function that is highly resilient to noise. Comprehensive evaluations of this method have been conducted on multiple datasets, including Flickr8k, Flickr30k, and MS-COCO, which have shown the substantial superiority of the proposed Collaborative Distillation approach over existing methods both in terms of performance and ability to resist noisy captions.
